https://dailytrust.com/lai-mohammed-comm.body: Former Minister of Information and Culture and Special Adviser to the United Nations World Tourism Organisation, Mr. Lai Mohammed, has commended the Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of the Nigerian Railway Corporation (NRC), Dr. Kayode Opeifa, for his ongoing efforts towards repositioning the Corporation and revitalising railway transportation in Nigeria. Mohammed gave the commendation during a courtesy visit to the NRC Legacy Museum in Lagos on Monday, October 19, 2026, where he emphasised the strategic importance of railway transportation to national development and the need to preserve Nigeria’s rich railway heritage for future generations. The former Minister, who was received by the Director of Operations, NRC, Mr. Akin Oshinowo, representing the Managing Director, alongside members of the Legacy Museum management team, described the ongoing transformation efforts within the Corporation as commendable. He encouraged Dr. Opeifa to remain steadfast in his determination to move the Corporation forward, noting that meaningful institutional transformation requires commitment, resilience, courage and individuals who are genuinely passionate about achieving results. According to him, the railway sector remains a critical component of Nigeria’s transportation infrastructure, with enormous potential to stimulate economic activities, facilitate the movement of people and goods, and contribute significantly to national development. He further stressed the importance of preserving the historical identity of the Nigerian railway system, observing that the sector’s rich heritage represents an important aspect of the country’s transportation history. Mohammed equally encouraged the management of the NRC Legacy Museum to sustain its efforts towards preserving historical artefacts, documents and other materials that reflect the evolution of railway transportation in Nigeria. He noted that beyond preserving history, the museum has the potential to serve as an important centre for education, tourism, research and public enlightenment, particularly for younger generations seeking to understand the contributions of rail transportation to Nigeria’s socioeconomic development. Earlier in his welcome remarks, the President of the NRC Legacy Museum, Mr. Taiye Olaniyi, expressed appreciation to the former Minister for finding time to visit the facility. Olaniyi explained that the museum was established to preserve and showcase the Corporation’s historical achievements while connecting the past, present and future of railway transportation in Nigeria. He noted that the museum houses historical materials and artefacts that provide valuable insights into the evolution of railway operations, infrastructure development and the contributions of railway transportation to the growth of communities and commercial activities across the country. Also speaking, the Director of Operations, Mr. Akin Oshinowo, who represented the NRC Managing Director, conveyed Dr. Opeifa’s warm greetings and appreciation to Mohammed for his interest in the Corporation and its historical heritage. Oshinowo noted that the Managing Director holds the former Minister in high regard and appreciates his continued interest in initiatives capable of promoting Nigeria’s cultural and transportation heritage. He expressed optimism that the visit would further draw attention to the tourism potential of the railway sector, particularly in the areas of heritage preservation, educational tourism and public engagement. The Director reiterated the Corporation’s commitment to improving railway service delivery while ensuring that its rich institutional history is adequately preserved and promoted. The highlight of the visit was a guided tour of the Legacy Museum, during which Mohammed was taken through various sections of the facility and acquainted with historical exhibits depicting the development and contributions of railway transportation in Nigeria. The visit also brought renewed attention to the opportunities available for integrating railway heritage into Nigeria’s tourism development initiatives, particularly through the promotion of historical railway facilities and educational excursions. For the Nigerian Railway Corporation, the visit represents another opportunity to strengthen stakeholder relationships and showcase the railway sector not only as an essential means of transportation but also as an important part of Nigeria’s cultural and industrial heritage. Under the leadership of Dr. Kayode Opeifa, the Corporation continues to pursue initiatives aimed at improving operational efficiency, enhancing passenger experience, strengthening stakeholder engagement and repositioning railway transportation as a dependable contributor to national economic development. The NRC remains committed to preserving its historical legacy while advancing its mandate of providing safe, reliable, efficient and customer-focused railway services across the country. https://dailytrust.com/lai-mohammed-comm.title_zh: 拉伊·穆罕默德赞扬奥佩法推动铁路转型，并要求保护尼日利亚铁路公司的文化遗产
https://dailytrust.com/lai-mohammed-comm.body_zh: 前信息与文化部长、联合国世界旅游组织特别顾问 Lai Mohammed 先生赞扬了尼日利亚铁路公司（NRC）董事兼首席执行官 Kayode Opeifa 博士，称他持续努力推动公司重新定位，并振兴尼日利亚铁路运输。Mohammed 于2026年10月19日星期一在拉各斯对 NRC 遗产博物馆进行礼节性访问时作出上述评价。他强调，铁路运输对国家发展具有战略意义，尼日利亚有必要为子孙后代保护其丰富的铁路遗产。前部长由代表董事的 NRC 运营总监 Akin Oshinowo 先生以及遗产博物馆管理团队成员接待。Mohammed 表示，公司内部正在推进的转型工作值得肯定。他鼓励 Opeifa 博士坚定不移地推动公司发展，并指出，切实推动机构转型需要投入、坚韧、勇气，以及真正渴望取得成果的人士。他说，铁路仍是尼日利亚交通基础设施的关键组成部分，具有巨大潜力，能够带动经济活动，便利人员和货物流动，并为国家发展作出重大贡献。他还强调保护尼日利亚铁路系统历史身份的重要性，指出该行业丰富的遗产是尼日利亚交通史的重要组成部分。Mohammed 同时鼓励 NRC 遗产博物馆管理层继续努力，保护能够反映尼日利亚铁路运输发展的历史文物、文件及其他资料。他表示，博物馆不仅能够保存历史，也有潜力成为教育、旅游、研究和公众启蒙的重要中心，尤其有助于年轻一代了解铁路运输对尼日利亚社会经济发展的贡献。在欢迎辞中，NRC 遗产博物馆馆长 Taiye Olaniyi 先生对前部长拨冗参观该设施表示欢迎和感谢。Olaniyi 表示，博物馆的设立旨在保护和展示公司的历史成就，同时连接尼日利亚铁路运输的过去、现在与未来。他说，博物馆收藏的历史资料和文物，为人们了解铁路运营演变、基础设施发展，以及铁路运输对全国各地社区增长和商业活动所作的贡献提供了宝贵视角。代表 NRC 董事出席的运营总监 Akin Oshinowo 先生也发言，转达 Opeifa 博士对 Mohammed 的热烈问候和感谢，感谢他关注公司及其历史遗产。Oshinowo 表示，董事非常敬重这位前部长，并感谢他持续关注能够 promoting 尼日利亚文化和交通遗产的各项举措。他乐观地认为，此次访问将进一步提升外界对铁路行业旅游潜力的关注，尤其是在遗产保护、教育旅游和公众参与等领域。该总监重申，公司致力于改善铁路服务，同时确保其丰富的机构历史得到充分保护和推广。本次访问的重头戏是对遗产博物馆进行导览参观。参观过程中，Mohammed 参观了馆内不同区域，并了解了展示尼日利亚铁路运输发展及其贡献的历史展品。此次访问还再次引发了人们对将铁路遗产融入尼日利亚旅游发展举措之机遇的关注，包括推广历史铁路设施和组织教育考察活动。对尼日利亚铁路公司而言，此次访问是加强利益相关方关系、展示铁路行业重要性的又一机会。铁路不仅是一种不可或缺的交通方式，也是尼日利亚文化和工业遗产的重要组成部分。在 Kayode Opeifa 博士的领导下，公司继续推进相关举措，以提高运营效率、改善乘客体验、加强利益相关方参与，并将铁路运输重新定位为国家经济发展中值得信赖的推动力量。NRC 致力于保护其历史遗产，同时履行在全国各地提供安全、可靠、高效且以客户为中心的铁路服务的使命。加入 Daily Trust WhatsApp 社区，快速获取身边的新闻与动态

https://www.myjoyonline.com/goldbod-to-h.title: GoldBod to help establish gold processing centres to improve traceability
https://www.myjoyonline.com/goldbod-to-h.summary: The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) is collaborating with the government to establish gold processing centres for small-scale mining cooperatives, in a move aimed at improving the traceability of gold purchased from miners. The proposed facilities are expected to help authorities verify the origins of gold entering the formal supply chain and address concerns about whether the mineral purchased by GoldBod comes from legitimate mining operations.
https://www.myjoyonline.com/goldbod-to-h.summary_zh: 加纳黄金局（GoldBod）正与政府合作，为小型矿业合作社建立黄金加工中心，以提升所采购黄金的可追溯性。拟建的设施有望帮助主管部门核实进入正式供应链的黄金来源，并回应外界对GoldBod所购矿产是否来自合法采矿作业的关切。
https://www.myjoyonline.com/goldbod-to-h.body: The Ghana Gold Board (GoldBod) is collaborating with the government to establish gold processing centres for small-scale mining cooperatives, in a move aimed at improving the traceability of gold purchased from miners. The proposed facilities are expected to help authorities verify the origins of gold entering the formal supply chain and address concerns about whether the mineral purchased by GoldBod comes from legitimate mining operations. The government is engaging private investors to support the initiative, with some proposals already received. The first processing centres are expected to be rolled out in the first quarter of 2027. GoldBod has expressed interest in facilitating the establishment of some of the facilities, with traceability identified as a key reason for its involvement in the project. “Why? Because the issue of traceability comes up any time we talk about gold that is being purchased by GoldBod. So, they are also interested in ensuring that we put in place a platform that will ensure that whatever gold that they buy can be traced to the right source. And so, we are collaborating with them,” he explained. The Deputy Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Dr Yusif Sulemana, disclosed the plans in an interview with Channel One TV on the sidelines of the Mining in Motion Summit in Accra. He said GoldBod had indicated its interest in supporting the process. “GoldBod has expressed interest in facilitating the process of establishing some of these processing centers,” he said. Beyond traceability, the centres are expected to improve gold recovery rates for small-scale miners and reduce their reliance on mercury and cyanide, which pose environmental risks. The initiative forms part of broader efforts to formalise small-scale mining through cooperative schemes, strengthen oversight of the gold supply chain and encourage more environmentally responsible mining practices
https://www.myjoyonline.com/goldbod-to-h.title_zh: 加纳黄金局将协助设立黄金加工中心，以提高可追溯性
https://www.myjoyonline.com/goldbod-to-h.body_zh: 加纳黄金局（GoldBod）正与政府合作，为小规模采矿合作社设立黄金加工中心，旨在提高从矿工处采购黄金的可追溯性。拟议中的设施预计将帮助当局核实进入正规供应链的黄金来源，并回应有关GoldBod采购的矿产是否来自合法采矿作业的担忧。政府正在接触私人投资者以支持这项倡议，目前已收到一些方案。首批加工中心预计将于2027年第一季度投入运营。GoldBod表示有兴趣协助设立其中部分设施，并将提高可追溯性列为参与该项目的主要原因。他解释道：“为什么这么说？因为每当我们谈到GoldBod采购黄金时，可追溯性问题都会被提及。因此，他们也希望确保我们建立一个平台，使他们采购的任何黄金都能追溯到正确的来源。因此，我们正在与他们合作。”土地与自然资源部副部长Yusif Sulemana博士在接受Channel One TV采访时，于阿克拉举行的Mining in Motion Summit边披露了这些计划。他说，GoldBod已表示有兴趣支持这一进程。他表示：“GoldBod已表示有兴趣协助推进其中部分加工中心的设立进程。”除提高可追溯性外，这些中心预计还将提高小规模采矿者的黄金回收率，并减少他们对汞和氰化物的依赖，因为这些物质会带来环境风险。该倡议是通过合作社计划推动小规模采矿正规化、加强黄金供应链监管以及促进更加 environmentally responsible 的采矿实践的更广泛努力的一部分。

https://leadership.ng/nasarawa-floods-go.title: Nasarawa Floods: Government To Relocate Communities As Victims Recount Losses
https://leadership.ng/nasarawa-floods-go.summary: The Nasarawa State Government has announced plans to relocate flood-prone riverine communities to higher ground as victims of recent flooding in Doma Local Government Area count their losses and await relief materials. More than a week after the floods killed two people and displaced over 4,000 others across 11 communities, many victims remain in neighbouring upland settlements without adequate food, clean water and medical supplies, LEADERSHIP reports.
https://leadership.ng/nasarawa-floods-go.summary_zh: 纳萨拉瓦州政府宣布，计划将易受洪水侵袭的河岸社区迁往地势较高地区；多马地方政府辖区的近期洪灾受害者正在清点损失，等待救援物资。洪水导致2人死亡、11个社区逾4000人流离失所一周多后，许多受害者仍居住在邻近高地定居点，缺乏充足的食物、清洁水和医疗用品，《领导力》报道称。
https://leadership.ng/nasarawa-floods-go.body: The Nasarawa State Government has announced plans to relocate flood-prone riverine communities to higher ground as victims of recent flooding in Doma Local Government Area count their losses and await relief materials. More than a week after the floods killed two people and displaced over 4,000 others across 11 communities, many victims remain in neighbouring upland settlements without adequate food, clean water and medical supplies, LEADERSHIP reports. The affected communities are Olegokemi, Obendo, Achebe, Olegopa, Oguatema, Ijiwo, Taliga, Otia, Otiageke, Otiagiso, Olegambulu and Anaguga. The director-general of the Nasarawa State Emergency Management Agency (NSEMA), Barrister Ben Akwash, said the government was planning to establish safer settlements for riverine communities, beginning with Umasha in Toto Local Government Area. The proposed settlements, being championed by the Ministry of Environment, would include basic amenities and storage facilities for valuables and foodstuffs. Construction is expected to begin after the rainy season. “We have concluded arrangements. We’re only waiting for the rains to recede. By the next rainy season, God willing, it will be a different ball game,” Akwash said. However, victims of the latest disaster say their immediate needs remain unmet as they struggle to rebuild their lives. In Ijiwo, 60-year-old widow Mrs Emun Agaba Enah said she had lost her livestock, chickens and farmlands, leaving her unable to provide for her children and six grandchildren. “Where do you think I should run to with six grandchildren and four of my own children?” she asked. Mr Ngbede said 34 other widows in the community had lost their livelihoods, while eight houses were completely washed away. Seventy-year-old Esther Achi, who could not flee when the flood reached Otariga, described the disaster as one of the worst in the area. “I’m old enough to die. Some of us can no longer run from this,” she said, pointing to the partly collapsed house of one of her sons. The lawmaker representing Doma South in the Nasarawa State House of Assembly, Musa Ibrahim Abubakar, urged the government to provide immediate relief, warning that shortages of clean water, food and medical supplies could trigger cholera and other waterborne diseases. “The people have lost their source of livelihood; the source of their drinking water is gone. Farmlands have been washed away, and all the drainages are silted,” he said during a motion on the disaster. Some residents and the lawmaker blamed the flooding on water released from the Lagdo Dam in Cameroon. However, the Nigeria Hydrological Services Agency (NiHSA) dismissed reports of a release on August 30, 2026, saying the dam was impounding water. NiHSA Director-General Umar Mohammed attributed flooding in the Benue River Basin to intense or prolonged rainfall, poor drainage, improper waste disposal and unauthorised construction. Meanwhile, Emmanuel Ogiri of Olegopa, who was displaced with six family members, said victims were still waiting for promised assistance despite visits by government officials, non-governmental organisations and emergency agencies. “They only said they would come back, but they are yet to return,” he said. Ogiri said he had returned to rebuild two of the four family houses destroyed by the flood. He added that schools and public infrastructure across the affected communities had also suffered damage. He said residents needed alternative land and government assistance to relocate safely. “If today government is able to allocate a parcel of land with support in terms of items that will enable us to put up a shelter upland, why not?” he asked. Raymond Achi of Obendo community said residents had repeatedly appealed for relocation but had received no response. On the delay in delivering relief materials, Akwash said the government had procured supplies but was struggling to transport them because roads to the affected communities were flooded. He said the route through Doma was difficult to navigate, while the alternative through Makurdi, Benue State, required boats to reach some communities. “We are looking to use several Hilux vehicles. By tomorrow, we would have taken the relief materials,” he assured. Akwash added that NSEMA’s relief stocks had been depleted earlier in the year following interventions in other flood-affected areas. The Speaker of the Nasarawa State House of Assembly, Danladi Jatau, urged the government to provide relief materials and deploy health workers to prevent disease outbreaks. He also called for collaboration with the National Emergency Management Agency (NEMA) to secure additional assistance. Jatau directed the Assembly’s Committees on Environment and Humanitarian Services to visit the affected communities and submit their findings within one week. The absence of official displacement camps has further worsened victims’ plight. Many are staying with relatives and residents of unaffected upland communities. “Victims are scattered and not in one place,” said Sunday Ijiwo, a resident of Ijiwo. Akwash confirmed that no official camp had been established, explaining that the disaster occurred suddenly. He said displaced residents were sheltering in places of worship, schools and host communities. https://leadership.ng/nasarawa-floods-go.body_zh: 纳萨拉瓦州政府宣布，计划将易受洪水侵袭的河岸社区迁往地势较高地区；Doma地方政府辖区的近期洪灾受害者正在清点损失，等待救援物资。洪水导致2人死亡、11个社区逾4,000人流离失所，逾一周后，LEADERSHIP报道，许多受害者仍居住在邻近的高地安置点，缺乏充足的食物、清洁饮用水和医疗用品。受影响社区包括Olegokemi、Obendo、Achebe、Olegopa、Oguatema、Ijiwo、Taliga、Otia、Otiageke、Otiagiso、Olegambulu和Anaguga。纳萨拉瓦州应急管理局（NSEMA）总检察长Ben Akwash表示，政府正计划为河岸社区建立更安全的安置点，首先从Toto地方政府辖区的Umasha开始。由环境部推动拟建安置点将配备基本设施，并设置 valuables和食品储存设施。工程预计于雨季结束后开工。Akwash说：“我们已经完成各项安排，只等雨水退去。到下一个雨季，若承蒙上帝眷顾，情况就会完全不同。”然而，最新一轮灾害的受害者表示，他们设法重建生活，但眼前需求仍未得到满足。60岁的寡妇Emun Agaba Enah在Ijiwo说，她失去了牲畜、鸡和农田，已无力抚养自己的4个孩子和6个孙辈。她问道：“你觉得我带着6个孙辈和自己4个孩子还能逃到哪里去？”Ngbede先生表示，社区另有34名寡妇失去生计来源，另有8栋房屋被洪水彻底冲毁。70岁的Esther Achi在洪水抵达Otariga时无法逃离，她称这场灾害是该地区最严重的灾害之一。她说：“我已经老到可以死了。我们有些人再也逃不动了。”她指向其中一个儿子部分坍塌的房屋。纳萨拉瓦州议会代表Doma South的议员Musa Ibrahim Abubakar敦促政府立即提供救济，并警告清洁饮用水、食物和医疗用品短缺可能引发霍乱及其他水媒疾病。他在议会就灾害提出动议时表示：“人们失去了谋生来源，饮用水源也没了。农田被冲毁，所有排水沟都淤塞了。”部分居民和该议员将洪灾归咎于喀麦隆Lagdo大坝放水。然而，尼日利亚水文局（NiHSA）否认了有关大坝于2026年8月30日放水的报道，称大坝当时正在蓄水。NiHSA总干事Umar Mohammed表示，贝努埃河流域洪灾源于强降雨或持续降雨、排水不畅、不当倾倒废物以及未经许可的建设。与此同时，Olegopa的Emmanuel Ogiri与6名家人流离失所，他说，尽管政府官员、非政府组织和应急机构到访过，受灾者仍在等待承诺的援助。他说：“他们只是说还会再来，但至今没有回来。”Ogiri说，他已返回重建被洪水摧毁的4栋家庭住宅中的2栋。他补充说，受影响社区的学校和公共基础设施也遭到破坏。他表示，居民需要替代土地和政府援助，以实现安全搬迁。他问道：“如果今天政府能够划拨一块地，并提供物品支持，让我们在高地搭建住所，为什么不呢？”Obendo社区的Raymond Achi表示，居民曾多次要求搬迁，却始终没有得到回应。对于救援物资迟迟未送达，Akwash表示，政府已经采购物资，但通往受影响社区的道路被洪水淹没，运输困难。他说，经Doma的路线难以通行，而经贝努埃州Makurdi的替代路线则需要乘船才能抵达部分社区。Akwash保证：“我们正考虑使用数辆Hilux车辆。明天就会把救援物资送到。”他补充说，今年早些时候，NSEMA曾前往其他受洪水影响地区开展救援，安置的物资已经耗尽。纳萨拉瓦瓦州议会议长Danladi Jatau敦促政府提供救援物资并派遣卫生工作者，以防止疾病暴发。他还呼吁与国家应急管理局（NEMA）协作，争取更多援助。Jatau指示议会环境委员会和人道主义服务委员会前往受影响社区，并在1周内提交调查结果。官方安置营地的缺失进一步加重了受害者的困境，许多人只能与亲属或未受洪水影响的高地社区居民同住。Ijiwo居民Sunday Ijiwo说：“受灾者分散各处，没有集中安置。”Akwash确认尚未设立官方营地，并解释说灾害突然发生，流离失所者只能暂时栖身在宗教场所、学校和接待社区。与此同时，Ngbede表示，生活条件恶化，正迫使一些受害者返回被洪水摧毁的家园，尽管这会带来疾病暴发风险。抢先掌握资讯。实时报道、突发独家消息和深度视角将直接发送到您的手机。不要满足于过时新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS的WhatsApp，随时获取全天候更新 →

https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.body: Core sector industries output, as measured by the Index of Core Industries (ICI) stood at 7.9% in September, up from 5.9% in August, according to data released by Ministry of Commerce and Industry on Wednesday. September output was the highest growth in the new ICI series, which has 2022-23 as its base year. Out of the nine industries in the index, six recorded expansion while the rest contracted. The industries that drove ICI growth were iron ore, electricity, coal, and refinery products. Iron ore output picked up pace in September, growing by 18.4% after rising by 5.5% in August. Since January this year, the sector has recorded double-digit growth in every month except February and August. Electricity, which has the highest weight of 31% in the index, grew by 11.4%, lower than the 13.2% recorded in the previous month. Coal output expanded by 10.7%, after contracting by 3.8% in the previous month. Refinery products, with the second-highest weight at 23%, also recorded a double-digit growth of 10.3% in September, compared with 5.6% in August. Cement and steel output grew by 4.9% and 9.8%, respectively. “Coal and iron ore output witnessed a meaningful pickup in their YoY growth rates in September 2026 compared to August 2026; while this was aided by a low base, the sequential uptick in coal was quite strong, amid low stocks at power plants,” said Aditi Nayar, chief economist at ICRA Ltd. “Growth in electricity generation eased somewhat to 11.4% in September 2026 from 13.1% in August 2026, albeit remaining quite strong, as the monsoon deficit supported demand in the month,” Nayar added. The sub-sectors that contracted in August were fertilisers, natural gas and crude oil. Fertilisers output saw the deepest contraction of 11.7% in the index in August, though it has improved from 12.4% contraction observed in last month. Natural gas output contracted by 4.6%, followed by crude oil which contracted 1.4%. The contractions in both natural gas and crude oil output narrowed compared to August. The contraction in these three industries would likely be because of shortage of raw materials because of ongoing West-Asia war, as India imports these raw materials. To be sure, crude oil and natural gas output remained negative even before the war started. Out of the 30-month data available from April 2024 in the new series, crude oil and natural gas were in contraction in 28 and 27 months, respectively. While fertilisers output remained in contraction for only twelve months. The overall index recorded cumulative growth of 5.1% in the current fiscal year (April-September), up from 2.5% in the same period of the previous year

https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.body_zh: 印度商工部周三发布的数据显示,以核心行业指数(ICI)衡量的核心行业产出在9月份达到7.9%,高于8月份的5.9%。9月份的产出是新核心行业指数系列(以2022—23财年为基期)中最高的增速。该指数涵盖九个行业,其中六个行业产出扩张,其余出现收缩。拉动核心行业指数增长的行业包括铁矿石、电力、煤炭和炼油产品。铁矿石产出在9月份加快增长,同比增长18.4%,而8月份为增长5.5%。自今年1月以来,除2月和8月外,该行业每月都录得两位数增长。在指数中权重最高(占31%)的电力产出增长11.4%,低于上月的13.2%。煤炭产出在上月收缩3.8%之后扩张了10.7%。权重第二高(占23%)的炼油产品在9月份也录得10.3%的两位数增长,8月份为5.6%。水泥和钢铁产出分别增长4.9%和9.8%。ICRA有限公司首席经济学家阿迪提·纳亚尔表示:"2026年9月煤炭和铁矿石产出的同比增长较2026年8月明显加快;虽然这得益于较低的基数,但在电厂库存偏低的情况下,煤炭的环比上升势头相当强劲。"纳亚尔补充说:"2026年9月发电增速从2026年8月的13.1%略微放缓至11.4%,但仍保持强劲,因当月季风不足支撑了需求。"上月出现收缩的子行业为化肥、天然气和原油。化肥产出在9月份出现指数中最深的收缩,降幅达11.7%,不过较上月12.4%的降幅有所改善。天然气产出收缩4.6%,随后是原油产出收缩1.4%。天然气和原油产出的降幅较8月份均有所收窄。这三个行业出现收缩可能是因为正在进行的西亚战争导致原材料短缺,因为印度依赖进口这些原材料。值得注意的是,即便在战争开始之前,原油和天然气产出也一直为负。在新系列自2024年4月起的30个月数据中,原油有28个月处于收缩状态,天然气有27个月处于收缩状态。而化肥产出仅有12个月处于收缩状态。本财年(4月至9月)该指数累计录得5.1%的增长,高于去年同期的2.5%……

Unlock these with Subscription Missiles struck Kyiv throughout the night, authorities said early on Thursday (October 22, 2026), sending residents into shelters and wounding six shortly after Russia signaled it was ready to resume trilateral talks with Ukraine and the United States. U.S. President Donald Trump said after his envoy Steve Witkoff's meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday (October 21) that it was "the closest we've been" to ending the war. Mr. Witkoff praised Mr. Putin as a "humanitarian" for freeing U.S. citizen Stephen Hubbard, but the Kremlin warned after the meeting in Saint Petersburg that while Moscow was "in principle" willing to restart talks there was little "substance" in Ukrainian and European peace proposals the U.S. diplomat had delivered. Attacks did not let up overnight, with Kyiv's Mayor Vitali Klitschko posting on social media that missile strikes had wounded six people in the capital, four of whom needed hospitalisation. Ukraine's Airforce posted a warning in the early hours of "more ballistic missiles towards Kyiv" and instructed residents to stay in shelters. Russian authorities also said they had intercepted drones during the night, including more than 160 flying towards Moscow. Mr. Witkoff had flown to Russia from a meeting with Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Oslo on Tuesday (October 20), which was aimed at smoothing over a bitter rift between Mr. Trump and the Ukrainian leader. Mr. Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner also took part in the talks with Mr. Putin remotely. Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov told reporters that Russia was "in principle, ready to resume" trilateral talks in mid-November — after crucial U.S. midterm elections — and that the Kremlin wanted them to focus on post-war security. Mr. Putin, who ordered the February 2022 invasion of Ukraine, has consistently rejected face-to-face talks with Mr. Zelenskyy and insisted Moscow intends to seize the rest of east Ukraine. Mr. Ushakov said Mr. Witkoff briefed Mr. Putin on "some new aspects in the approaches of the Europeans and Kyiv" from the Oslo meeting, adding though that "there wasn't really much substance in them". A summit between Mr. Putin, Mr. Trump, and China's Xi Jinping was also being prepared in China's Shenzhen for next month, Mr. Ushakov said, calling it "the first such meeting in history." During their three-hour meeting, Mr. Witkoff praised Mr. Putin for granting Mr. Trump's request to free Hubbard, a retired English teacher in his 70s who had always denied the charges he was a "mercenary" fighting for Ukraine. "You talk so much about my President, President Trump, being a humanitarian — you are a humanitarian also, sir, and I salute that," Mr. Witkoff said. Mr. Witkoff said on social media that the talks with Mr. Putin were "constructive" but that "there is still important work left to do". Discussions would continue between the U.S., Ukraine, and Russia at the technical level, he added. Mr. Trump returned to power in January 2025 promising to end the war in 24 hours — but more than a year of U.S.-led talks have failed to produce a breakthrough, with tens of thousands killed. In recent days, a frustrated Mr. Trump has once again pivoted away from Ukraine and back to Mr. Putin, trumpeting what he said was a deal for Russia to sell diesel and reduce prices sent soaring by his Iran war. Mr. Trump also delayed the imposition of sanctions on Russia's war machine — a decision he defended on Wednesday (October 20) as necessary to secure Hubbard's release. "If you would've put those sanctions on... you could forget about him. You'd never see him again," Mr. Trump told reporters at the White House. In Ukraine, Mr. Zelenskyy said that Kyiv also backed resuming trilateral talks. "The American side is proposing to organize this meeting as soon as possible. We are in favour of it," he told journalists. Mr. Witkoff's ninth meeting with Mr. Putin came as Russia continued to strike Ukrainian cities ahead of winter. Kyiv said Russian attacks killed at least four people on Wednesday (October 21) — including two in the capital and an elderly couple in the eastern Kharkiv region. Russian occupation authorities in the Lugansk region, meanwhile, said a Ukrainian drone strike on a phone company had killed two people. The Witkoff-Zelenskyy meeting on Tuesday (October 20) followed days of friction between Washington and Kyiv, and calls from Mr. Trump for the Ukrainian leader to be replaced. Mr. Witkoff told Mr. Putin he saw "some degree of momentum" in the U.S.-led talks. The U.S. envoy also told Mr. Putin that Washington was "grateful" for the diesel deal, which sparked outrage in Kyiv and across Europe. The deal has been seen as a way to try to lower fuel prices for American consumers ahead of the U.S. midterms, in which Mr. Trump's Republicans could lose control of Congress. https://www.thehindu.com/news/internatio.body_zh:

当局于2026年10月22日星期四一大早表示，导弹整夜袭击基辅。在俄罗斯表示准备恢复与乌克兰和美国的三方会谈后不久，袭击造成6人受伤，迫使居民进入避难所。美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周三（2026年10月21日）与其特使史蒂夫·维特科夫会见俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京后称，这是“我们距离结束战争最近的一次”。维特科夫称赞普京释放了美国公民斯蒂芬·哈伯德，并称他是一位“人道主义者”；但克里姆林宫在圣彼得堡会谈后警告称，尽管莫斯科“原则上”愿意重启会谈，但这名美国外交人员转交的乌克兰和欧洲和平方案仍鲜有“实质内容”。

整夜袭击并未停止。基辅市长维塔利·克利奇科在社交媒体上发文称，导弹袭击在首都造成6人受伤，其中4人需要住院。乌克兰空军在凌晨发布警报，称“有更多弹道导弹飞向基辅”，并要求居民留在避难所。俄罗斯当局也表示，夜間拦截了多架无人机，其中包括飞往莫斯科的160多架无人机。

维特科夫周二（2026年10月20日）在奥斯陆与乌克兰总统沃洛迪米尔·泽连斯基会面后飞往俄罗斯。此次会面旨在弥合特朗普与这位乌克兰领导人之间的严重裂痕。特朗普的女婿贾里德·库什纳也远程参加了与普京的会谈。

克里姆林宫官员尤里·乌沙科夫对记者表示，俄罗斯“原则上已准备好在11月中旬恢复三方会谈”，时间安排在美国重要的中期选举之后。克里姆林宫希望会谈聚焦于战后安全问题。普京于2022年2月下令入侵乌克兰，此后一直拒绝与泽连斯基面对面会谈，并坚持称莫斯科打算夺取乌克兰东部其余地区。

乌沙科夫说，维特科夫向普京介绍了奥斯陆会面中“欧洲人和基辅在处理方式上的若干新层面”，但他补充称，“这些方案并没有多少实质内容”。乌沙科夫还表示，普京、特朗普和中国国家主席习近平的峰会也在筹备之中，拟于下个月在中国深圳举行，并称这将是“历史上首次此类会面”。

在长达3小时的会谈中，维特科夫称赞普京答应特朗普的请求，释放了哈伯德。哈伯德是一名年逾七旬的退休英语教师，他始终否认自己作为“为乌克兰作战的雇佣兵”所受的指控。维特科夫说：“你们如此谈论我的总统特朗普总统，称他是一位人道主义者——先生，您同样是一位人道主义者，我对此表示敬意。”

维特科夫在社交媒体上表示，与普京的会谈“富有建设性”，但“仍有重要工作要做”。他补充说，美国、乌克兰和俄罗斯将在技术层面继续讨论。

特朗普于2025年1月重返白宫，承诺在24小时内结束战争，但美国主导的会谈持续一年多仍未取得突破，已有数万人死亡。近几天，沮丧的特朗普再次把注意力从乌克兰转向普京，大力宣传他所说的俄罗斯出售柴油、压低因他对伊朗发动战争而飙升的价格的交易。

特朗普还推迟了对俄罗斯战争机器实施制裁。他周三（2026年10月20日）为这一决定辩护称，此举是确保哈伯德获释所必需的。特朗普在白宫对记者说：“如果你实施那些制裁……你就别指望能见到他了。你永远不会再见到他。”

在乌克兰，泽连斯基表示基辅也支持恢复三方会谈。他对记者说：“美国方面提议尽快组织这次会面。我们对此表示赞成。”

维特科夫与普京第九次会面之际，俄罗斯在冬季来临前持续打击乌克兰城市。基辅表示，俄罗斯的袭击周三（2026年10月21日）造成至少4人死亡，其中包括首都的2人死亡，以及哈尔科夫地区一对老年夫妇。与此同时，卢甘斯克地区的俄罗斯占领当局表示，乌克兰无人机袭击一家电话公司，造成2人死亡。

维特科夫与泽连斯基周二（2026年10月20日）的会面，发生在华盛顿与基辅连续数日发生摩擦，以及特朗普要求更换这位乌克兰领导人之后。维特科夫告诉普京，他看到美国主导的会谈出现了“某种程度的动力”。这名美国特使还告诉普京，华盛顿对柴油交易表示“感激”，但该交易在基辅和欧洲各地引发愤怒。各方将这项交易视为美国中期选举前设法降低美国消费者燃油价格的一种手段。在此次选举中，特朗普所属的共和党可能失去对国会的控制。

https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.body: With the next hearing in an alleged conspiracy case involving seven foreign nationals who trained ethnic militias in Myanmar after travelling there via India scheduled for Friday, all eyes are on whether US national Mathew Aaron VanDyke will return to India. People close to VanDyke, who did not want to be named, said he would return to India and join the court proceedings on Friday since he had already booked his return ticket from the US. However, the National Investigation Agency (NIA), which is probing the case, is waiting for a confirmation from VanDyke. “He is expected to come back and attend the next court date - set on Friday,” one of them said. HT is trying to get in touch with VanDyke’s family in the US. VanDyke and six Ukrainian nationals – arrested in March this year under stringent provisions of the Unlawful Activities Prevention Act or UAPA that were later dropped by the agency in its charge sheet filed in September – were allowed by a Delhi court to return to their countries in the last week of September for a month on a condition that they will rejoin the investigations. The seven accused were only charged under the Immigration and Foreigners Act, which is a compounding offence, by NIA in its charge sheet. The federal agency did not press for their physical presence in India despite keeping its UAPA probe against them open, and agreed on their travel back home after they furnished personal undertakings, and provided their residential address and contact details. VanDyke was arrested on March 13 at Kolkata airport under section 18 of the UAPA, which relates to conspiracy, advocacy, abetment or incitement to commit a terrorist act. The six Ukrainians – Hurba Petro, Taras Slyviak, Ivan Sukmanovskyi, Marian Stefankiv, Maksim Honcharuk and Viktor Kaminskyi – were arrested at Delhi and Lucknow airports the same day. NIA had earlier alleged the seven accused had illegally entered Myanmar through Mizoram without valid travel documents and participated in a pre-scheduled training programme for Myanmar-based ethnic armed groups targeting the Myanmar military junta. The US national is being represented by advocates Rohit Gour and Rohit Dandriyal. They are yet to comment on his return. NIA has alleged that for nearly three months, the seven accused imparted training in drone warfare, drone operations, assembly and jamming technology to members of Myanmar-based ethnic armed groups, including the Chin National Front (CNF) and the Kachin Independence Army (KIA). It has also claimed that VanDyke and others received logistical support from the members of CNF and the mission was financed through funds arranged by a commander of a Myanmar-based rebel group. NIA has so far not commented on the return of the accused to their countries
https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.title_zh: 美国籍国民范戴克会返回印度吗？法院周五审理与缅甸无人机战争有关的案件
https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.body_zh: 一宗据称涉及7名外国公民的阴谋案下一次听证会定于周五举行；这7人经印度前往缅甸，在那里培训了民族民兵。所有人的目光都聚焦在美国公民Mathew Aaron VanDyke是否会返回印度。VanDyke身边不愿具名的人士表示，他将在周五返回印度并参加庭审，因为他已经预订了从美国返回的机票。不过，负责调查此案的印度国家调查局（NIA）仍在等待VanDyke的确认。其中一人说：“预计他会回来出席定于周五的下一次开庭。HT正在设法联系VanDyke在美国的家人。VanDyke和6名乌克兰公民今年3月依据《非法活动防止法》（UAPA）的严格条款被捕，但该机构在9月提交的起诉书中撤销了这些指控。德里法院允许他们在9月最后一周返回各自国家一个月，前提是他们必须重新参加调查。NIA在起诉书中仅依据《移民和外国人法》对这7名被告提出指控，该法涵盖可加重处罚的罪行。尽管对他们的UAPA调查仍在继续，这家联邦机构没有要求他们本人留在印度；在他们提交个人承诺、住所地址和联系方式后，该机构同意他们返回各自国家。VanDyke于3月13日在加尔各答机场依据UAPA第18条被捕，该条涉及策划、宣传、协助或煽动实施恐怖行为。这6名乌克兰人——Hurba Petro、Taras Slyviak、Ivan Sukmanovskyi、Marian Stefankiv、Maksim Honcharuk和Viktor Kaminskyi——于同一天在德里和勒克瑙机场被捕。NIA此前指控，7名被告未持有效旅行证件，经米佐拉姆非法进入缅甸，并参加了面向以缅甸为基地、针对缅甸军事委员会武装的民族武装组织的预先安排培训计划。这名美国公民由Rohit Gour和Rohit Dandriyal律师代理。他们尚未就其是否返回发表评论。NIA指控，近3个月来，7名被告向以缅甸为基地的民族武装组织成员培训无人机战争、无人机操作、组装和干扰技术；这些组织包括钦族民族阵线（CNF）和克钦独立军（KIA）。NIA还声称，VanDyke等人获得了CNF成员的后勤支持，行动资金由一个总部位于缅甸的叛乱组织指挥官筹措。NIA迄今没有就被告返回各自国家一事发表评论

https://www.chinadailyasia.com/article/6.title: China, Russia eye ties in AI, other frontier sectors
https://www.chinadailyasia.com/article/6.summary: China and Russia have agreed to foster new drivers of development in frontier areas such as artificial intelligence, biotechnology and the digital economy, in addition to advancing cooperation in key traditional sectors, according to a meeting between the two countries' heads of government.
https://www.chinadailyasia.com/article/6.summary_zh: 中俄两国政府首脑会晤后宣布，双方将在人工智能、生物技术和数字经济等前沿领域培育新的发展动能，同时深化在传统重点领域的合作。
https://www.chinadailyasia.com/article/6.body: China and Russia have agreed to foster new drivers of development in frontier areas such as artificial intelligence, biotechnology and the digital economy, in addition to advancing cooperation in key traditional sectors, according to a meeting between the two countries' heads of government. Premier Li Qiang , who co-chaired the 31st regular meeting with Russian Prime Minister Mikhail Mishustin in St. Petersburg on Wednesday, said that China and Russia, faced with a complex and turbulent international landscape in recent years, "have stood shoulder to shoulder and moved forward in unity" under the strategic guidance of the two countries' heads of state. Through dynamic and resilient cooperation, the two sides have managed to offset the impact of instability and external uncertainties and broaden bilateral cooperation, Li said, noting that the China-Russia strategic partnership of coordination for the new era is entering a new phase, marked by greater achievements and faster development. China is willing to work with Russia to build on the spirit of mutual respect and mutual benefit, and to promote even deeper and more substantive cooperation in various fields, Li said. China also stands ready to work with Russia to better translate the important consensus reached by the two heads of state into concrete actions and tangible outcomes, better serve the development and revitalization of both countries, and bring greater benefits to the two peoples, he added. This year marks the 25th anniversary of the signing of the China-Russia Treaty of Good-Neighborliness and Friendly Cooperation. Mishustin said the bilateral relationship is currently at its highest level in history and serves as a model for relations between countries. Despite uncertainties in the international landscape, Russia-China economic and trade cooperation has maintained sound momentum, he said. Russia is willing to work with China on the basis of mutual benefit, win-win cooperation, mutual respect and good-neighborliness and friendship, in order to further strengthen practical cooperation in various fields and safeguard the common interests of the two countries, he added. After the meeting, Li and Mishustin signed a joint communique, and the two sides agreed on cooperation documents covering a wide range of areas. The Chinese Foreign Ministry said that both sides agreed to "advance cooperation in key areas such as trade, economy, investment, energy, resources, connectivity, aerospace, finance and industry". According to the Chinese embassy in Russia, the value of bilateral trade surpassed $185 billion in the first eight months of 2026, up 28.4 percent year-on-year. As part of a fresh consensus reached at the meeting, the two sides underlined the need to ensure the success of the "China-Russia Year of Education", strengthen people-to-people exchanges in tourism, culture, youth and media, and stimulate the vitality of local cooperation. China and Russia also agreed to maintain close communication and coordination on multilateral affairs and strive to reach more practical outcomes. Li and Mishustin heard reports from representatives of several China-Russia bilateral cooperation committees and affirmed the work of these committees over the past year. The committees cover investment cooperation, energy cooperation, people-to-people and cultural exchanges, regular meetings between heads of government, and intergovernmental cooperation between China's Northeast and Russia's Far East
https://www.chinadailyasia.com/article/6.title_zh: 中国和俄罗斯着眼于人工智能及其他前沿领域的合作
https://www.chinadailyasia.com/article/6.body_zh: 中国和俄罗斯已同意在人工智能、生物技术和数字经济等前沿领域培育新的发展动力，同时推进各重点传统领域的合作，这是两国政府首脑会晤时透露的信息。国务院总理李强周三在圣彼得堡与俄罗斯总理米哈伊尔·米舒斯京共同主持了第31次中俄总理定期会晤。李强表示，面对近年来复杂动荡的国际形势，中俄在两国元首的战略引领下"肩并肩团结前行"。李强说，通过富有活力和韧性的合作，双方成功抵消了不稳定和外部不确定因素带来的影响，并拓展了双边合作。他指出，中俄新时代全面战略协作伙伴关系正进入新阶段，成果更加丰硕，发展更加迅速。李强表示，中方愿与俄方一道，本着相互尊重、互利共赢的精神，推动各领域合作走深走实。李强还表示，中方愿同俄方一道，更好地将两国元首达成的重要共识转化为具体行动和切实成果，更好服务于两国的发展振兴，为两国人民带来更大福祉。今年是中俄睦邻友好合作条约签署25周年。米舒斯京表示，两国关系正处于历史最高水平，堪称国与国关系的典范。他说，尽管国际形势存在不确定性，俄中经贸合作仍保持良好势头。米舒斯京还说，俄方愿同中方在互利共赢、相互尊重、睦邻友好的基础上，进一步加强各领域务实合作，维护两国的共同利益。会晤后，李强和米舒斯京签署了联合公报，双方就涵盖广泛领域的合作文件达成一致。中国外交部表示，双方同意"推进贸易、经济、投资、能源、资源、互联互通、航空航天、金融、工业等重点领域的合作"。据中国驻俄罗斯大使馆介绍，2026年前8个月双边贸易额超过1850亿美元，同比增长28.4%。作为本次会晤达成的新共识的一部分，双方强调要确保"中俄教育年"活动取得成功，加强旅游、文化、青年和媒体领域的人文交流，激发地方合作活力。中俄还同意在多边事务中保持密切沟通协调，争取取得更多务实成果。李强和米舒斯京听取了多个中俄双边合作委员会代表的工作汇报，对各委员会过去一年的工作予以肯定。这些委员会涵盖投资合作、能源合作、人文交流、总理定期会晤以及中国东北与俄罗斯远东地区间政府间合作……

Unlock these with Subscription The Trump administration is asking a federal judge to let it reconsider a major federal permit granted for a large offshore wind farm, making it the fourth project the Republican leadership has targeted in recent months. The Interior Department wants to reconsider its own approval for the "construction and operations plan" for the New England Wind project off Massachusetts. The plan was approved in 2024 during the Biden administration. The Justice Department said in a filing on Tuesday (October 20, 2026) that the Court should send the permit back to Interior, because the plan was approved despite major adverse impacts. Sen. Sheldon Whitehouse, a Rhode Island Democrat, warned that the administration now risks derailing a legislative effort to speed up permitting reviews for new energy and infrastructure projects. The Senate reached a bipartisan deal in September on a permitting bill, which has not yet been voted on. "This is how you blow up a permitting deal," he said in a statement on Wednesday (October 21, 2026). The Trump administration is using executive orders, agency actions and the courts to try to stop the development of offshore wind, a technology that President Donald Trump has attacked as "ugly" and unreliable compared to fossil fuels such as coal and natural gas. Officials started buying back offshore wind leases after federal judges blocked its efforts to stop construction on five major East Coast projects. The Interior Department also wants to reconsider its prior approval of the construction and operations plan for Revolution Wind, a wind farm for Rhode Island and Connecticut that has finished construction, and for the Maryland Offshore Wind Project, which has not yet begun construction. In August, a judge granted the administration's request to reconsider the permit for the stalled New Jersey project Atlantic Shores. That project had been halted soon after Mr. Trump returned to office because co-owner Shell walked away from it. Last year, a federal judge said the Trump administration could reconsider the permit granted to the Massachusetts project SouthCoast Wind days before the President's inauguration to a second term. Pasha Feinberg, an offshore wind strategist at the Natural Resources Defence Council, said the Trump administration's attacks on offshore wind are escalating at a time when Americans are struggling with surging utility bills. "It's long past time for the Trump administration to realise its war on clean energy is backfiring," Mr. Feinberg said. The National Ocean Industries Association, which represents offshore industries including oil and wind, said it's concerned about the uncertainty that comes with reopening federal approvals for offshore energy projects, particularly those already under construction or in operation. "The Senate has made meaningful progress on deep reforms that would provide greater certainty for energy projects across the board," said the association's president, Erik Milito. The administration's actions "underscore why Congress needs to get this done", he said. The plans for New England Wind call for up to 129 wind turbines that could supply as much as 2,600 megawatts of clean energy to power more than 900,000 homes each year. The developer, Avangrid, declined to comment on Wednesday (October 21, 2026). Construction has not begun. The project's federal approval was challenged in court by ACK for Whales, a group of Nantucket, Massachusetts, residents who say they are concerned about the negative impacts of offshore wind development. The lawsuit in District Court for the District of Columbia contends that the federal government failed to comply with numerous statutes. The federal defendants in the case filed a motion on Tuesday (October 20, 2026) stating that remand of the permit is warranted, so Interior could make a new decision. The government also told the Court in 2025 it wanted to reconsider New England Wind's approval. Interior said in a statement on Wednesday (October 21, 2026) that the latest filing complied with a briefing schedule and was not announcing a policy change. Its position on offshore wind has remained consistent throughout this administration, the statement said. Avangrid built another wind farm, Vineyard Wind, off the coast of Massachusetts in a joint venture with Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners. Construction finished in March, making it the first project to reach this stage during Mr. Trump's time in office. https://www.thehindu.com/news/internatio.body_zh: 订阅账户还可享受独家报道、社论、观点等更多内容。订阅即可解锁这些内容。特朗普政府正向一名联邦法官提出请求，要求允许其重新审议为一座大型海上风电场签发的重大联邦许可证；这是共和党领导层近几个月瞄准的第四个项目。内政部希望重新审议其自身对马萨诸塞州近海“New England Wind”项目建设与运营计划的批准。该计划于2024年拜登政府执政期间获批。司法部在2026年10月20日星期二提交的一份文件中表示，法院应将许可证发回内政部，因为该计划尽管存在重大不利影响仍获批准。罗德岛州民主党参议员Sheldon Whitehouse警告称，该政府如今可能破坏一项旨在加快新能源和基础设施项目许可审查的立法努力。参议院于9月就一项许可法案达成两党协议，但尚未进行表决。他在2026年10月21日星期三的一份声明中表示：“这就是你们破坏许可协议的方式。”特朗普政府正利用行政命令、机构行动和法院，试图阻止海上风电的发展；特朗普总统曾批评这项技术“丑陋”，并认为其相较煤炭和天然气等化石燃料并不可靠。在联邦法官阻止政府试图叫停东海岸五个大型项目建设后，官员们开始回购海上风电租约。内政部还希望重新审议此前对Revolution Wind项目建设与运营计划的批准。该风电场位于马萨诸塞州近海，为马萨诸塞州和康涅狄格州供电，现已完成建设；内政部也希望重新审议尚未开工的Maryland Offshore Wind Project的批准。8月，一名法官批准了政府重新审议陷入停滞的新泽西州项目Atlantic Shores许可证的请求。由于共同所有者Shell退出，该项目在特朗普先生重返白宫后不久便告停工。去年，一名联邦法官表示，特朗普政府可以重新审议总统就职数日前授予马萨诸塞州项目SouthCoast Wind的许可证，以开启第二任期。自然资源保护协会海上风电策略师Pasha Feinberg表示，在美国民众艰难应对公用事业账单飙升之际，特朗普政府对海上风电的攻击正在升级。Feinberg先生说：“特朗普政府早就应该意识到，他对清洁能源发动的战争正在适得其反。”全国海洋工业协会代表包括石油和风能在内的海洋产业，该协会表示，重新审议海上能源项目联邦批准所引发的不确定性令人担忧，尤其是对已处于建设或运营阶段的项目而言。该协会会长Erik Milito表示：“参议院在深入改革方面已取得实质性进展，这些改革将为所有能源项目提供更大的确定性。”他说，政府的行动“凸显了国会为何必须完成这项工作”。New England Wind计划安装最多129台风力涡轮机，每年可提供最多2,600兆瓦清洁能源，为超过900,000户家庭供电。开发商Avangrid在2026年10月21日星期三拒绝置评。项目尚未开工。马萨诸塞州Nantucket居民组成的“ACK for Whales”在法院对该项目的联邦批准提出挑战，称他们担心海上风电开发带来的不利影响。这起诉讼由哥伦比亚特区地区法院审理，诉称联邦政府未遵守多项法规。案件中的联邦被告于2026年10月20日星期二提交动议，称有理由将许可证发回重审，以便内政部作出新决定。政府还在2025年告知法院，希望重新审议New England Wind的批准。内政部在2026年10月21日星期三的一份声明中表示，最新文件符合简报提交时间表，并不代表政策变化。声明称，本届政府对该海上风电的立场始终如一。Avangrid曾与Copenhagen Infrastructure Partners成立合资企业，在马萨诸塞州近海建设另一座风电场Vineyard Wind。该项目于3月完工，成为特朗普先生任内首个进入这一阶段的项目。Vineyard Wind是政府曾试图叫停建设的项目之一，政府以国家安全受到威胁为由作出该决定。评论必须使用英文，并以完整句子表达。评论不得含有辱骂性内容或针对个人。请遵守我们的社区评论准则。我们已迁移至新的评论平台。如果你已是The Hindu注册用户并已登录，可以继续参与文章讨论。如尚无账户，请注册并登录后发表评论。用户登录账户后可在Vuukle查看以前的评论

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/22/f.title: FG, SATH to Develop Tech Innovation Ecosystem for Global Competitiveness
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/22/f.summary: The federal government, through the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) and the SATH Foundation, is collaborating with industry stakeholders to develop technology innovation ecosystem for Nigeria that will form a benchmark for global competitiveness in the technology space.
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/22/f.summary_zh: 联邦政府通过国家信息技术发展局和SATH基金会，正与行业利益相关者合作，为尼日利亚开发技术创新生态系统，这将成为全球技术领域竞争力的基准。
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/22/f.body: The federal government, through the National Information Technology Development Agency (NITDA) and the SATH Foundation, is collaborating with industry stakeholders to develop technology innovation ecosystem for Nigeria that will form a benchmark for global competitiveness in the technology space. Driven by NITDA, and with a committee already put in place to enhance the initiative, NITDA, in Lagos, presented a pilot report of the committee’s TechOutlook 2026, which covered five key sectors that include: Financial Services, Telecommunications, Commerce & Trade, Government Services and Healthcare. “Nigeria needs to develop a globally competitive innovation ecosystem, because we cannot build a globally competitive innovation ecosystem on assumptions, or on data guessing or relying on international estimation, industry reports, and individual successes. Nigeria needs to build ecosystem intelligence, technology intelligence, to drive global competitiveness. Such tech ecosystem will help investors to easily identify opportunities for investment. It will help government to redirect policies. It will help innovators to identify emerging technologies and challenges that need solutions,” Abdullahi said. Chairman, SATH Foundation, Collins Onuegbu, in his welcome address, said the idea behind TechOutlook was to build a national platform where the people shaping Nigeria’s technology future could meet each year, take an honest look at where we are, anticipate what is coming, and agree on the priorities that require us to act together. According to him, TechOutlook is designed in such a way that SATH Foundation will continue as a delivering and managing partner, while NITDA and the industry will collaborate in joint ownership and stewardship through a strategic partnership. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/22/f.title_zh: 联邦政府与SATH合作开发技术创新生态系统以提升全球竞争力
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/22/f.body_zh: 联邦政府通过国家信息技术发展局（NITDA）和SATH基金会，正与产业利益相关方合作，为尼日利亚打造技术创新生态系统，这将成为尼日利亚在技术领域具备全球竞争力的基准。在NITDA的主导下，已成立一个委员会来加强这项举措，NITDA在拉各斯发布了该委员会《TechOutlook 2026》试点报告，报告涵盖五个关键部门，包括：金融服务、电信、商业与贸易、政府服务和医疗保健。“尼日利亚需要打造一个具有全球竞争力的创新生态系统，因为我们不能基于假设、数据猜测或依赖国际估算、行业报告以及个别成功案例来构建具有全球竞争力的创新生态系统。尼日利亚需要构建生态系统情报和技术情报，以驱动全球竞争力。这样的技术生态系统将帮助投资者轻松识别投资机会。它将帮助政府重新调整政策。它将帮助创新者识别新兴技术和需要解决方案的挑战，”阿卜杜拉希说。SATH基金会主席Collins Onuegbu在欢迎致辞中表示，TechOutlook背后的理念是建立一个国家平台，让塑造尼日利亚技术未来的人们能够每年相聚，诚实地审视我们所处的位置，预测即将发生的事情，并就要求我们共同行动的优先事项达成一致。据他介绍，TechOutlook的设计方式是SATH基金会将继续作为交付和管理伙伴，而NITDA和产业界将通过战略伙伴关系在共同所有权和监管方面进行合作。THISDAY创刊于1995年1月22日，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕克里克路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都区及世界各地设有办事处。它是尼日利亚最具权威性的新闻媒体，在所有平台上为政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶级提供服务，同时作为新思想、文化和技术与有抱负者和千禧一代的交汇点。该报是一家致力于追求真理和理性的公共信托机构，报道范围从突发新闻到政治、商业、市场、艺术、体育和社区，以及人与社会的交汇点。您可以通过hello@thisdaylive.com与我们联系，或访问我们的联系页面。

https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/22/a.body: Abbey Bank Plc has said it is targeting growth following approval by the Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) to convert to a regional commercial bank. Formerly known as Abbey Mortgage Bank Plc, the bank said the commencement of commercial banking in the fourth quarter of 2026 is a milestone that marks a significant evolution for the institution, building on more than three decades of experience in mortgage financing, real estate development and customer-focused financial services. Commenting on the Bank’s transformation, its Managing Director/Chief Executive Officer, Mobolaji Adewumi, said, their ambition is to make banking more accessible, responsive and relevant to the aspirations of individuals, families and businesses. According to him, “The year 2026 represents a defining moment in the history of Abbey. Our approval to transition to commercial banking is a testament to the work invested in building this institution and the confidence placed in us by our regulators, shareholders, customers and employees. “We are building on more than three decades of experience, particularly in mortgage banking and real estate finance, while preparing to serve a broader range of financial needs. Our ambition is to make banking more accessible, more responsive and more relevant to the aspirations of individuals, families and businesses. “The transition represents more than a change in licence or name. It signals Abbey’s ambition to expand access to financial services, deepen customer relationships and create greater opportunities for individuals, businesses and communities. It also builds on years of experience in mortgage banking and real estate finance, providing a foundation for the Bank to broaden its capabilities and pursue new opportunities within Nigeria’s financial services sector,” he stressed. He noted that Abbey’s transformation is underpinned by a focus on financial resilience, sustainable growth and capital strengthening. “The Bank recorded strong financial momentum in 2025, with pre-tax profit rising to N3.12 billion from N1.22 billion in 2024. This performance provides an important foundation as the institution prepares for the opportunities and responsibilities associated with commercial banking.Digital banking remains a central pillar of Abbey’s strategy to make financial services more accessible, convenient and responsive to customers’ everyday needs,” he said. https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/22/a.title_zh: 阿贝银行在启动商业银行业务之际瞄准增长
https://www.thisdaylive.com/2026/10/22/a.body_zh: 阿贝银行股份有限公司表示，在获得尼日利亚中央银行（CBN）批准转为区域商业银行后，该行正瞄准增长。此前名为阿贝抵押银行股份有限公司，该银行称2026年第四季度启动商业银行业务是一个里程碑，标志着该机构在抵押融资、房地产开发和以客户为中心的金融服务领域积累超过三十年经验后实现重大演进。在评论该银行转型时，其董事总经理兼首席执行官莫博拉吉·阿德伍米表示，他们的抱负是让银行业务对个人、家庭和企业的愿望更加易于获得、更加响应迅速且更加相关。据他介绍，“2026年代表着阿贝历史上一个决定性时刻。我们获批转型为商业银行，证明了我们在建设这一机构方面所投入的工作，以及监管机构、股东、客户和员工对我们的信心。“我们正在三十多年经验的基础上继续前进，特别是在抵押银行和房地产融资领域，同时准备服务更广泛的金融需求。我们的抱负是让银行业务对个人、家庭和企业的愿望更加易于获得、更加响应迅速且更加相关。“这一转型不仅仅是牌照或名称的改变。它标志着阿贝扩大金融服务获取渠道、深化客户关系并为个人、企业和社区创造更多机会的抱负。它还建立在多年抵押银行和房地产融资经验的基础上，为该银行拓宽能力并在尼日利亚金融服务部门追求新机会提供了基础，”他强调。他指出，阿贝的转型以注重财务韧性、可持续增长和资本强化为基础。“该银行在2025年录得强劲财务势头，税前利润从2024年的12.2亿奈拉增至31.2亿奈拉。这一业绩为该机构准备迎接与商业银行业务相关的机会和责任提供了重要基础。数字银行仍是阿贝战略的核心支柱，旨在让金融服务对客户的日常需求更加易于获得、更加便捷且更加响应迅速，”他说。作为商业银行筹备工作的一部分，阿贝也在推进技术。该报于1995年1月22日创立，由THISDAY NEWSPAPERS LTD.出版，地址为尼日利亚拉各斯阿帕帕克里克路35号，在尼日利亚36个州、联邦首都特区及世界各地设有办事处。它是尼日利亚最具权威性的新闻媒体，在所有平台上为政治、商业、专业和外交精英以及更广泛的中产阶级提供服务，同时作为新思想、文化和技术对有抱负者和千禧一代的交汇点。该报纸是一种公共信托，致力于追求真相和理性，报道从突发新闻到政治、商业、市场、艺术、体育、社区以及人与社会交汇点的一系列议题。您可以通过hello@thisdaylive.com与我们联系，或访问我们的联系页面。

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/prot.title: Protection, Not Prosecution: Why Nigeria must decriminalise attempted suicide
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/prot.summary: An inconsistent legal framework When a human being reaches a point of acute psychological anguish where they attempt to end their life, the immediate imperative of any just, constitutional state must be protection, not prosecution. The recent advancement of a bill seeking to decriminalise attempted suicide and establish a national framework for suicide prevention, which passed its second reading in the Senate this week, marks a critical legislative watershed.
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/prot.summary_zh: 不一致的法律框架 当一个人陷入剧烈的心理痛苦以致试图结束生命时，任何公正的宪政国家的当务之急必须是保护而非起诉。本周在参议院通过二读的法案旨在将企图自杀行为去罪化并建立全国自杀预防框架，这标志着一个关键的立法转折点。
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/prot.body: The National Suicide Prevention Bill, 2026 offers the Senate an opportunity to align Nigerian law with its human rights obligations and with the evidence on suicide prevention. That opportunity should not be lost. On 13 October 2026, the Senate passed the National Suicide Prevention Bill, 2026 (SB. 730) on second reading. During the debate, the Senate President, Senator Godswill Akpabio, opposed the bill’s central reform, reportedly stating: “If you attempt suicide, make sure you die. Anyone who attempts and fails will go to jail.” The remark has understandably drawn public concern. More importantly, it reflects a view that still underpins our criminal law: that a person who survives a suicide attempt should be met with punishment rather than care. From a human rights perspective, that position is difficult to reconcile with Nigeria’s constitutional and international obligations. As the bill moves to committee, it is worth setting out why. An inconsistent legal framework When a human being reaches a point of acute psychological anguish where they attempt to end their life, the immediate imperative of any just, constitutional state must be protection, not prosecution. Yet, for decades, Nigeria’s statutory legal framework has treated deep personal crisis as a criminal act. Under Section 327 of the Criminal Code and Section 231 of the Penal Code, individuals who survive a suicide attempt face up to one year in prison (both provisions derive from colonial-era legislation; the United Kingdom repealed the equivalent offence through the Suicide Act 1961). This punitive approach creates a stark legal contradiction with the National Mental Health Act, which rightly recognises attempted suicide as a psychiatric emergency requiring medical care and psychosocial support. Nigerian law therefore currently treats the same individual as both a patient in need of urgent care and an offender liable to prosecution. The recent advancement of a bill seeking to decriminalise attempted suicide and establish a national framework for suicide prevention, which passed its second reading in the Senate this week, marks a critical legislative watershed. Sponsored by Senator Asuquo Ekpenyong (Cross River South), the bill placed a fundamental human rights question before the nation: when a Nigerian survives a suicide attempt, should the state’s first response be prosecution or protection? The bill resolves this inconsistency. Clause 18 repeals both provisions. Part II sets out the rights of persons who have attempted suicide, including confidentiality, informed consent, access to legal representation and protection from torture and cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment. The bill also provides for a Suicide Prevention Unit, national and state surveillance systems, 24-hour crisis helplines and mandatory training for health workers, law enforcement and correctional personnel. The bill drew support from several senators. Senator Dayo Faduyile, a medical doctor, noted that some survivors have subsequently died by suicide while in detention. The bill has been referred to the Committees on Health and on Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters for a public hearing. Nigeria’s human rights obligations The question is not solely one of health policy. Nigeria has accepted binding obligations that bear directly on it. UN Special Rapporteurs on the right to health and on torture have found the criminalisation of suicide attempts inconsistent with these obligations, noting that the detention of persons in acute distress may engage the prohibition of cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment. The World Health Organization identifies decriminalisation as a critical step towards the Sustainable Development Goal target of reducing suicide mortality by one third by 2030. From an international human rights and legal standpoint, penalising attempted suicide is fundamentally flawed, counterproductive, and inconsistent with Nigeria’s treaty obligations under international law. The evidence on criminalisation World Health Organization estimates cited during the Senate debate place suicide deaths in Nigeria at approximately 16,000 per year. Practitioners regard this as a conservative figure, since fear of prosecution and stigma lead families to conceal both attempts and deaths. Overcoming the misconception of deterrence Arguments suggesting that criminal sanctions act as a “deterrent” against suicide stem from a fundamental misunderstanding of mental health dynamics and international human rights principles. Suicidal behaviour is not a calculated criminal offence; it is an indicator of unaddressed psychological distress, socio-economic hardship, or deep-seated trauma. Countries across the world that have repealed legacy criminal provisions and replaced them with evidence-based mental health support, crisis response systems, and mandatory psychosocial assessment have seen improved mental health outcomes without an increase in suicide rates. Federal and state competence The Senate President and the Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele, raised legitimate questions about the bill’s application across states, given that the Penal Code operates as state law in the North. This is a matter for careful drafting and consultation, not a reason for delay. The National Assembly should lead, and State Houses of Assembly should be engaged to undertake corresponding reforms. The path forward: transforming legislative debate into legal legacy As the bill moves to the Committees on Health and on Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters for public hearings and stakeholder engagement, Nigerian lawmakers must prioritise constitutional rights, international standards, and public health over archaic penal logic. Decriminalisation does not mean the state is indifferent to suicide; rather, it shifts the state’s response from the criminal justice system to the public health framework. To build a comprehensive protective framework, Nigeria needs to: Repeal Section 327 of the Criminal Code and Section 231 of the Penal Code in full, without substituting any alternative sanction, to align national legislation with the National Mental Health Act. Establish national prevention pathways: fund operational crisis helplines, community mental health care, and specialised training for law enforcement officers, teachers, and healthcare workers to serve as first responders. Decriminalisation without accessible care would be incomplete. Guarantee rights-based mental healthcare: Ensure that mental health interventions are accessible, voluntary, non-discriminatory, and rooted in human dignity. Involve the states: Invite State Houses of Assembly to the public hearing and agree to a framework for corresponding reform of state criminal laws. Hear affected voices: Listen directly to persons with lived experience, families and mental health professionals, consistent with the bill’s own provisions on the composition of the National Suicide Prevention Task Force. The Senate has taken an important first step. The committee stage is where that commitment will be tested. Nigeria should choose protection over prosecution and enact a law that treats survivors of suicide attempts with the dignity, compassion and care to which they are entitled. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/prot.body_zh: 2026年国家自杀预防法案为参议院提供了一个机会，使尼日利亚法律与其人权义务以及自杀预防的证据保持一致。这个机会不应错失。2026年10月13日，参议院二读通过了2026年国家自杀预防法案（SB. 730）。在辩论期间，参议院议长戈兹维尔·阿克帕比奥参议员反对该法案的核心改革，据称他表示：“如果你试图自杀，就确保你死掉。任何试图自杀但失败的人都将入狱。”这一言论理所当然地引起了公众担忧。更重要的是，它反映了一种仍然支撑我们刑法的观点：即自杀未遂的幸存者应该受到惩罚而不是得到照顾。从人权角度来看，这种立场难以与尼日利亚的宪法和国际义务相协调。随着法案进入委员会阶段，值得阐明原因。一个不一致的法律框架当一个人陷入极度心理痛苦以致试图结束生命时，任何公正的宪政国家的首要任务必须是保护，而不是起诉。然而，几十年来，尼日利亚的法定法律框架一直将严重的个人危机视为犯罪行为。根据《刑法典》第327条和《刑罚法典》第231条，自杀未遂的幸存者面临最高一年的监禁（这两项规定均源自殖民时代立法；联合王国通过1961年《自杀法案》废除了类似罪行）。这种惩罚性做法与《国家心理健康法案》形成鲜明法律矛盾，后者正确地将自杀未遂视为需要医疗护理和心理社会支持的精神病紧急情况。因此，尼日利亚法律目前将同一个人既视为需要紧急护理的患者，又视为可能被起诉的罪犯。本周在参议院二读通过的寻求将自杀未遂非罪化并建立国家自杀预防框架的法案，标志着一个关键的立法分水岭。该法案由克罗斯河州南区参议员阿苏库奥·埃克佩尼翁提出，将一个基本人权问题摆在全国面前：当一名尼日利亚人自杀未遂幸存时，国家的首要反应应该是起诉还是保护？该法案解决了这种不一致。第18条废除了这两项规定。第二部分规定了自杀未遂者的权利，包括保密性、知情同意、获得法律代理以及免受酷刑和残忍、不人道或有辱人格待遇的保护。该法案还规定设立自杀预防单位、国家和州监测系统、24小时危机热线以及对卫生工作者、执法人员和惩教人员的强制培训。该法案得到了几位参议员的支持。医学博士达约·法杜伊莱参议员指出，一些幸存者在拘留期间随后自杀身亡。该法案已移交卫生委员会以及司法、人权和法律事务委员会进行公开听证。尼日利亚的人权义务这个问题不仅仅是卫生政策问题。尼日利亚已接受了直接相关的具有约束力的义务。联合国健康权和酷刑问题特别报告员认定，将自杀未遂定为犯罪与这些义务不一致，并指出拘留处于严重痛苦中的人可能触及禁止残忍、不人道或有辱人格待遇的规定。世界卫生组织将非罪化确定为实现到2030年将自杀死亡率降低三分之一的可持续发展目标的关键步骤。从国际人权和法律角度来看，对自杀未遂进行惩罚在根本上是错误的、适得其反的，并且与尼日利亚根据国际法承担的条约义务不一致。关于罪化的证据参议院辩论中引用的世界卫生组织估计数字显示，尼日利亚每年自杀死亡人数约为16000人。从业者认为这是一个保守的数字，因为对起诉的恐惧和污名导致家庭隐瞒自杀未遂和死亡。克服威慑的误解认为刑事制裁对自杀起到“威慑”作用的论点源于对心理健康动态和国际人权原则的根本误解。自杀行为不是经过计算的犯罪行为；它表明存在未得到解决的心理困扰、社会经济困难或根深蒂固的创伤。世界各地废除遗留刑事规定并代之以基于证据的心理健康支持、危机应对系统以及强制心理社会评估的国家，在自杀率没有上升的情况下看到了心理健康成果的改善。联邦和州的能力参议院议长和参议院领袖奥佩耶米·巴米德莱参议员对该法案在各州的适用性提出了合理问题，因为《刑罚法典》在北方作为州法律运作。这是一个需要仔细起草和协商的问题，而不是拖延的理由。国民议会应发挥领导作用，各州议会应参与进行相应的改革。前进的道路：将立法辩论转化为法律遗产随着法案移交卫生委员会以及司法、人权和法律事务委员会进行公开听证和利益相关者参与，尼日利亚立法者必须优先考虑宪法权利、国际标准和公共卫生，而不是陈旧的刑罚逻辑。非罪化并不意味着国家对自杀漠不关心；相反，它将国家的反应从刑事司法系统转变为公共卫生框架。为了建立全面的保护框架，尼日利亚需要：全面废除《刑法典》第327条和《刑罚法典》第231条，而不代之以任何替代制裁，以使国家立法与《国家心理健康法案》保持一致。建立国家预防途径：资助运行中的危机热线、社区心理健康护理，并为执法人员、教师和医护人员提供专门培训，使其作为第一响应者。缺乏可及护理的非罪化将是不完整的。保障基于权利的心理健康护理：确保心理健康干预措施可及、自愿、非歧视，并植根于人的尊严。让各州参与：邀请各州议会参加公开听证，并商定州刑事法律相应改革的框架。听取受影响的声音：直接听取有亲身经历者、家庭和心理健康专业人士的意见，这与法案本身关于国家自杀预防工作队组成的规定一致。参议院已经迈出了重要的一步。委员会阶段将是这一承诺接受考验的地方。尼日利亚应选择保护而不是起诉，并制定一部法律，以幸存者应得的尊严、同情和关怀对待自杀未遂的幸存者。此处表达的评论不反映先锋报或其任何员工的意见

https://www.myjoyonline.com/a-case-for-a.summary_zh: 加纳政府最近宣布推出一套新的道路交通法规，旨在遏制该国频繁发生的道路事故。政府必须采取分阶段、系统性的推出方式，优先处理致命违法行为，先建设基础设施，并教育广大公众，特别是直接受新规则影响的人，然后再处罚违规者。
https://www.myjoyonline.com/a-case-for-a.body: The Government of Ghana recently announced the rollout of a new set of road traffic regulations, aiming to curb the spate of road accidents in the country. Like any other efforts by previous administrations which sought to deal with the carnage on our roads, the new regulations could, by intent, be a positive move. The law must, however be rolled out systematically and implemented thoughtfully, else it is bound to fail. The regulations in question, ‘Road Traffic Regulations, 2026 (L.I. 2519)’, stand to fail if the government enforces all penalties simultaneously. The law, as has been put out, covers dozens of offences, from speeding to preaching in moving vehicles, with penalties that have jumped dramatically from what pertained in the old regulations. Three structural barriers make a “big bang” approach unworkable: Drivers are largely uninformed about the new rules, enforcement infrastructure is not ready, and compliance costs are stacking up. The government must adopt a phased, systematic rollou t that prioritizes fatal offences, builds infrastructure first, and educates the general public, and those the new rules affect directly in particular, before it penalizes offenders. Changes in the new L.I from the old law appear drastic. This amounts to a sweeping overhaul. The law covers offences ranging from street racing, jumping red lights, and failing to stop at STOP signs to parking in disabled designated spaces and unauthorised use of bus stops. Preaching or hawking in a moving commercial vehicle now also carries a jail term of three to eight months, up from the previous maximum of 30 days, while fines range from 5 penalty units to 200 penalty units, with one penalty unit valued at GH¢12 . What makes a law like this problematic is that, when you put these many behaviours together and criminalise them at once, you create a situation where a large portion of drivers are technically in violation of something. That undermines the moral authority of the law and makes selective enforcement inevitable. One key concern regarding the coming of this new road traffic law is that there has not been adequate public and stakeholder engagement. The Ghana Private Road Transport Union (GPRTU) has stated that its members were not consulted before the L.I was passed, and remain unaware of the new rules. How can drivers comply with a law they do not understand? The Ministry of Transport launched a nationwide education exercise in September 2026, with Transport Minister Joseph Bukari Nikpe acknowledging that nationwide education was “necessary to help drivers, transport operators, motor unions and other road users understand their responsibilities”. But one month of sensitization is certainly not enough time to absorb dozens of new offences and changed penalties. As the GPRTU has argued, drivers need to be properly educated before enforcement begins. Penalizing people for violations they did not know existed is not enforcement—it is ambush. It is a fact and legitimate argument to make also that the government has not put in place the needed infrastructure that will cater for effective implementation of the new law. CUTS International, a policy think tank, has publicly called on the government to delay full enforcement until traffic lights and road markings at enforcement locations have been inspected and repaired. Their concerns are specific: some traffic lights across Accra are obscured by overgrown trees, others are damaged or out of service. At some junctions, one of two traffic lights works while the other does not. Faded lane markings and stop lines make it impossible for drivers to know where they should stop. And, it is worth noting that the government itself has acknowledged the need for more preparation. The Ghana Police Service rescheduled the full implementation of TRAFFITECH-GH from October 1 to November 1, specifically to allow for “more extensive public awareness and education.” This postponement is tacit recognition that the original timeline was too aggressive. The compliance cost of new driver’s licence presents yet another element of challenge. The GPRTU has warned that the new licensing requirements could leave commercial drivers paying for up to three different licences—a professional driver’s licence, a separate commercial driver’s licence, and existing MMDA permits. The union’s deputy PRO pointed out: “It will not help businesses because if it happens like that, then it means we will be paying too much, increasing our operational cost”. The GPRTU opposes the auction provision, arguing that “nobody will intentionally leave his vehicle on the road”, and that owners should be allowed to reclaim vehicles after paying towing and storage fees. What happens in this circumstance is that when compliance costs rise sharply while enforcement expands simultaneously, drivers face a rational calculation: the cost of obeying may exceed the cost of violating. That is not a recipe for compliance. Statistically, the data on Ghana’s road accident deaths suggests the need for prioritization. Ghana recorded 2,949 road deaths in 2025, the highest in 35 years and an 18.2% increase over 2024. Speeding accounted for more than 60% of all collision s . Motorcycle crashes rose by 19.4%, with 6,548 motorcycles involved in crashes. If the government focuses enforcement resources on these killers—speeding, drunk driving, red-light running, motorcycle helmet use—the safety gains will be immediate and measurable. Spreading limited enforcement capacity across preaching, hawking, parking violations, and administrative offences dilutes the impact on what actually kills people. The police have already indicated that the initial phase of TRAFFITECH-GH will focus on speeding. This is the right instinct. It should be formalized into policy. To ensure effective implementation of the new road traffic regulations, enforce should focus strictly on offences with the clearest link to fatalities: speeding, red-light running, drunk driving, motorcycle helmet use, and seat belt use. These have the strongest public consensus and the highest safety return. An equally important measure is to include offences that require physical infrastructure to comply with, such as stopping at YIELD signs, pedestrian crossing rules, bus stop regulations. Here, the relevant infrastructure should be provided before enforcement. Where such infrastructure exists, it should be functional. The introduction of administrative and nuisance offences should come last. By that point drivers would have experienced a functioning system for about a year and understand the expectations. It is expected for some to argue that gradualism signals weakness—that the government is not serious, that indiscipline continues while authorities tiptoe. The 2,949 deaths demand urgency. But urgency does not require chaos. The government can signal seriousness by strictly enforcing a focused set of critical offences while phasing in the rest. Here the message becomes: “We are serious about saving lives, and we are doing this properly.” That is more credible than a blitz that collapses under its own weight, breeds corruption, and alienates the very drivers whose cooperation is essential. In all, L.I. 2519 contains the right intentions. But good intentions do not make good policy. A law that overwhelms the enforcement system, punishes drivers for infrastructure failures, and imposes costs that make compliance irrational will not save lives. It will generate resentment, bribery, and evasion. A systematic, phased approach—prioritizing fatal offences, building infrastructure first, and educating before penalizing—gives the law a chance to work. The goal is not to punish the maximum number of people. The goal is to reduce the 2,949 deaths. That requires strategy, not shock therapy. Before issuing any fine, there should be complete visibility inspections at every enforcement location. Repair obscured signals, repaint faded markings, install missing speed limit signs. There should be face-to-face education with commercial driver unions. Equally, there should be verification to ensure that the vehicles registration database can accurately identify offenders
https://www.myjoyonline.com/a-case-for-a.title_zh: 有必要系统推行加纳新交通法（L.I. 2519）
https://www.myjoyonline.com/a-case-for-a.body_zh: 加纳政府最近宣布推出一套新的道路交通法规，旨在遏制该国频繁发生的道路事故。与以往历届政府为处理道路惨剧所做的努力一样，新法规从意图上看可能是一项积极举措。然而，这项法律必须系统地推出并经过深思熟虑地实施，否则注定会失败。如果政府同时强制执行所有处罚条款，所涉及的《2026年道路交通法规（L.I. 2519）》将面临失败风险。该法律涵盖数十种违法行为，从超速到在行驶车辆中传教，处罚力度较旧法规大幅提高。三大结构性障碍使得“大爆炸”式推行方式不可行：司机大多对新规则不知情，执法基础设施尚未就绪，合规成本不断累积。政府必须采取分阶段、系统性的推出方式，优先处理致命违法行为，首先建设基础设施，并对公众尤其是直接受新规则影响的人进行教育，然后再处罚违规者。新法规与旧法相比的变化显得剧烈，这相当于一次全面改革。该法律涵盖的违法行为包括街头赛车、闯红灯、未在停止标志处停车、将车停在残疾人专用车位以及未经授权使用公交车站等。在行驶的商用车辆中传教或叫卖现在也将面临三个月至八个月的监禁，此前最高仅为30天，罚款范围从5个处罚单位到200个处罚单位不等，每个处罚单位价值12加纳塞地。像这样一部法律的问题在于，当你将如此多的行为放在一起并一次性将其刑事化时，就会造成大量司机在技术上违反某项规定的局面。这会削弱法律的道德权威，并使选择性执法不可避免。关于这部新道路交通法即将实施的一个关键担忧是，公众和利益相关方的参与度不足。加纳私营道路运输工会（GPRTU）表示，其成员在该法规通过前未被征求意见，并且仍然对新规则一无所知。司机如何遵守他们不理解的法律？交通部于2026年9月启动了全国教育行动，交通部长约瑟夫·布卡里·尼克佩承认，全国教育“对于帮助司机、运输经营者、机动车工会和其他道路使用者了解他们的责任是必要的”。但仅仅一个月的宣传教育肯定不足以消化数十种新违法行为和变更后的处罚。正如加纳私营道路运输工会所主张的，司机需要在执法开始前接受适当的教育。对人们不知道存在的违规行为进行处罚不是执法，而是伏击。政府尚未建立起必要的基础设施来有效实施新法，这也是一个事实和合理的论点。政策智库CUTS International已公开呼吁政府推迟全面执法，直到执法地点的交通信号灯和道路标线经过检查和修复。他们的担忧很具体：阿克拉的一些交通信号灯被茂密的树木遮挡，其他信号灯则损坏或无法使用。在某些路口，一组交通信号灯中只有一个正常工作而另一个不工作。褪色的车道标线和停止线使司机无法知道应该在哪里停车。而且值得注意的是，政府自己也承认需要更多准备。加纳警察局将TRAFFITECH-GH的全面实施从10月1日推迟到11月1日，专门为了进行“更广泛的公众意识和教育”。这一推迟默示承认原定时间表过于激进。新驾照的合规成本构成了另一个挑战因素。加纳私营道路运输工会警告说，新的许可要求可能导致商用司机需要支付多达三种不同的执照费用——专业司机执照、单独的商用司机执照以及现有的MMDA许可证。该工会副公共关系官员指出：“这不会对企业有帮助，因为如果这样的话，就意味着我们要支付太多费用，从而增加我们的运营成本”。加纳私营道路运输工会反对拍卖条款，认为“没有人会故意把自己的车辆留在路上”，车主在支付拖车和存放费用后应被允许取回车辆。在这种情况下，当合规成本急剧上升而执法同时扩大时，司机就会面临一个理性的计算：遵守的成本可能超过违规的成本。这不是实现合规的良方。从统计数据看，加纳道路事故死亡数据表明需要优先处理某些问题。加纳2025年录得2949例道路死亡，这是35年来的最高数字，比2024年增加了18.2%。超速占所有碰撞事故的60%以上。摩托车碰撞事故上升了19.4%，涉及6548辆摩托车。如果政府将执法资源集中在这些致命因素上——超速、酒驾、闯红灯、摩托车头盔使用——安全收益将是立竿见影且可衡量的。将有限的执法能力分散到传教、叫卖、停车违规和行政违规上，会削弱对真正致死因素的影响。警方已经表示，TRAFFITECH-GH的初始阶段将重点关注超速。这是正确的直觉，应该将其正式化成政策。为了确保新道路交通法规的有效实施，执法应严格聚焦于与致命事故关联最明确的违法行为：超速、闯红灯、酒驾、摩托车头盔使用以及安全带使用。这些行为拥有最强烈的公众共识和最高的安全回报。同样重要的措施是纳入那些需要物理基础设施才能遵守的违法行为，例如在让行标志处停车、行人过街规则、公交车站规定。在这种情况下，应先提供相关基础设施再进行执法。如果此类基础设施已经存在，则应确保其正常运行。行政和滋扰类违法行为的引入应放在最后。到那时，司机已经体验了约一年的正常运转系统并理解了预期。有些人可能会认为渐进式做法意味着软弱——即政府不够认真，在当局小心翼翼时无纪律行为仍在继续。2949例死亡要求采取紧急行动。但紧急行动并不需要混乱。政府可以通过严格执法一组重点关键违法行为，同时分阶段引入其余内容来表明其严肃态度。这样传递的信息就是：“我们认真对待拯救生命，并且正在以正确的方式做这件事。”这比一场因自身负担过重而崩溃、滋生腐败并疏远需要其配合的司机的突击行动更可信。总之，L.I. 2519包含了正确的意图。但良好的意图并不等于良好的政策。一部压垮执法系统、因基础设施故障而惩罚司机、并施加使合规变得不理性的成本的法律，不会拯救生命。它将产生怨恨、贿赂和逃避。一种系统的、分阶段的方法——优先处理致命违法行为，首先建设基础设施，并在处罚前进行教育——才能给这部法律一个发挥作用的机会。目标不是惩罚最多的人。目标是减少2949例死亡。这需要策略，而不是休克疗法。在发出任何罚款之前，应在每个执法地点进行全面可见度检查。修复被遮挡的信号灯，重新粉刷褪色的标线，安装缺失的限速标志。应与商用司机工会进行面对面的教育。同样，应进行验证以确保车辆登记数据库能够准确识别违规者。

https://leadership.ng/end-reliance-on-fg.summary: Senator Shettima stated this on Wednesday while declaring open the National Stakeholders’ Workshop on the Electricity Act 2023 at the State House Banquet Hall, Presidential Villa, Abuja. https://leadership.ng/end-reliance-on-fg.summary_zh: 谢蒂马参议员周三在阿布贾总统别墅国家宴会厅宣布全国利益相关者关于2023年电力法案研讨会开幕时发表了上述言论。副总统由总统副幕僚长易卜拉欣·哈桑·哈德吉亚参议员代表，他表示该法案创造了分散电力治理的机会，并使各州能够开发适合自身经济需求和可用资源的电力市场。
https://leadership.ng/end-reliance-on-fg.body: He said Nigeria’s ambition to build a competitive industrial economy would remain constrained unless electricity reforms translated into reliable power for businesses, households and public institutions across the country. Senator Shettima stated this on Wednesday while declaring open the National Stakeholders’ Workshop on the Electricity Act 2023 at the State House Banquet Hall, Presidential Villa, Abuja. According to a statement by his spokesman, Stanley Nkwocha, the workshop, themed: “Unlocking the Opportunities of the Electricity Act 2023 for Sustainable Energy Development and Economic Growth in Nigeria,” brought together federal and state institutions, regulators and other stakeholders to review the implementation of the legislation. Represented by Deputy Chief of Staff to the President, Senator Ibrahim Hassan Hadejia, the Vice President said the Act had created an opportunity to decentralise electricity governance and enable states to develop power markets suited to their economic needs and available resources. “The Act empowers States to develop and regulate intrastate electricity markets within the applicable constitutional and statutory framework. The size, diversity and endowments of this nation demand this decentralisation. “Electricity supply must become a shared responsibility, pursued with innovation and accountability across the Federation. Our States must shed the habit of waiting for Abuja to provide every answer,” he said. Senator Shettima identified the country’s diverse energy resources as a major opportunity for expanding electricity access, citing solar potential in Sokoto, Borno and Katsina, gas resources in Delta, Rivers and Bayelsa, and hydroelectric opportunities in Niger and Kebbi. He urged states to translate these advantages into investments capable of powering agriculture, manufacturing, healthcare and education. The Vice President, however, warned that legislation alone would not guarantee improved electricity supply, calling on states yet to establish their regulatory institutions to begin the process without delay. “Legislation cannot implement itself. States yet to act must begin their legislative and institutional preparations promptly. They need to establish functional electricity regulatory bodies with technical competence and capacity,” he said. To strengthen implementation, VP Shettima proposed a National Electricity Reform Peer Review and Implementation Framework involving the Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC), Federal Ministry of Power, Nigeria Governors’ Forum (NGF) and state electricity regulators. He explained that the proposed voluntary framework would allow states to exchange experiences, strengthen regulatory institutions and assess progress in market development, investment readiness, consumer protection and electricity access. “No State needs to purchase with failure the knowledge another State has already acquired,” he said. According to him, annual voluntary reviews should identify implementation challenges, facilitate technical assistance and promote practical solutions without undermining the constitutional powers of states. The Vice President also emphasised the importance of private sector participation, noting that government funding alone could not meet Nigeria’s electricity infrastructure requirements. “Government cannot finance this transformation from the treasury alone; private capital must arrive with technology and expertise. Transparent licensing, predictable regulation, commercially viable markets, investment safeguards and credible dispute resolution will earn investors’ confidence,” he stated. He reaffirmed President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s commitment to expanding electricity access through policies that encourage investment, strengthen institutions and improve service delivery. “Under His Excellency, President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, GCFR, the Federal Government will sustain policies and partnerships for accessible, reliable, efficient and progressively affordable electricity for households and businesses,” Senator Shettima said. He also called for stronger consumer safeguards against arbitrary billing, poor service and unfair commercial practices, insisting that electricity operators must be held accountable for service quality. “The final verdict on this law will be delivered wherever a Nigerian reaches for a switch. Entrepreneurs need dependable power, young Nigerians need employment, and investors need transparent rules under which enterprise can prosper,” he added. Earlier, the Permanent Secretary of the Federal Ministry of Power, Mahmuda Mamman, who represented the Minister of Power, said the success of the Electricity Act would depend on the capacity of states to establish credible institutions and commercially viable electricity markets. He noted that state-level electricity planning would allow governments to respond more effectively to local demand and infrastructure requirements. Also speaking, the Director-General of the Nigeria Governors’ Forum, Dr. Abdulateef O. T. Shittu, said the forum was working to strengthen coordination between federal and state institutions in implementing the legislation. He disclosed that efforts were underway to develop a standard tariff framework for states to protect consumers while promoting investment and commercial sustainability. Dr. Shittu urged stakeholders to ensure that any amendments to the existing legal framework strengthened progress already recorded in electricity regulation. In her remarks, the Deputy General Manager (Compliance) and Head of Compliance at NERC, Hauwa Yakubu, disclosed that the commission had issued regulatory transfers to 17 states, with Akwa Ibom being the most recent. She said the commission had continued to support emerging state electricity regulators through peer-to-peer training and technical engagement. According to her, the Electricity Act 2023 introduced a new era of multilevel electricity regulation, bringing regulatory responsibilities closer to consumers and allowing states to address their peculiar electricity challenges. https://leadership.ng/end-reliance-on-fg.body_zh: 他说，除非电力改革转化为全国企业和家庭及公共机构都能用上的可靠电力，否则尼日利亚建设具有竞争力的工业经济的雄心仍将受到制约。谢蒂马参议员周三在阿布贾总统别墅国家宴会厅宣布2023年电力法国家利益相关者研讨会开幕时作此表述。根据其发言人斯坦利·恩沃查发布的声明，这次以“释放2023年电力法为尼日利亚可持续能源发展和经济增长带来的机遇”为主题的研讨会汇聚了联邦和州级机构、监管部门及其他利益相关者，共同审议该立法的实施情况。副总统由总统副幕僚长易卜拉欣·哈桑·哈德吉亚参议员代表出席，他表示该法案创造了一个机会，可以实现电力治理的去中心化，并使各州能够开发适合自身经济需求和可用资源的电力市场。“该法案授权各州在适用的宪法和法定框架内开发和监管州内电力市场。这个国家的规模、多样性和禀赋要求实行这种去中心化。电力供应必须成为一项共同责任，在联邦范围内以创新和问责的方式加以推进。我们的各州必须改掉一切都等待阿布贾提供答案的习惯。”他说。谢蒂马参议员指出，该国多样化的能源资源是扩大电力供应的重大机遇，他列举了索科托、博尔诺和卡齐纳的太阳能潜力，三角洲、河流州和巴耶尔萨的天然气资源，以及尼日尔州和凯比州的水电机遇。他敦促各州将这些优势转化为能够为农业、制造业、医疗和教育提供动力的投资。不过，副总统警告说，仅靠立法本身并不能保证电力供应得到改善，他呼吁尚未建立监管机构的州立即启动这一进程。“立法不会自行实施。尚未采取行动的州必须立即开始立法和机构筹备工作。他们需要建立具备技术能力和容量的有效电力监管机构。”他说。为了加强实施工作，副总统谢蒂马提议建立一个由尼日利亚电力监管委员会（NERC）、联邦电力部、尼日利亚州长论坛（NGF）和州电力监管机构参与的国家电力改革同行审议和实施框架。他解释说，这个拟议的自愿框架将允许各州交流经验、加强监管机构并评估市场发展、投资准备、消费者保护和电力接入方面的进展。“任何州都不必用失败去购买另一个州已经获得的知识。”他说。据他介绍，每年一次的自愿审议应找出实施挑战、促进技术援助并推动实际解决方案，同时不削弱各州的宪法权力。副总统还强调了私营部门参与的重要性，指出仅靠政府资金无法满足尼日利亚的电力基础设施需求。“政府无法仅靠国库来资助这一转型；私人资本必须带着技术和专业知识到来。透明的许可、可预测的监管、商业上可行的市场、投资保障和可信的争议解决机制将赢得投资者的信心。”他表示。他重申博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努布总统通过鼓励投资、加强机构和改善服务交付的政策来扩大电力供应的承诺。“在博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努布总统阁下领导下，联邦政府将继续维持各项政策和伙伴关系，为家庭和企业提供可及、可靠、高效且逐步变得可负担的电力。”谢蒂马参议员说。他还呼吁加强对消费者的保护，防止出现任意计费、服务差和不公平商业行为的情况，坚决要求电力运营商必须对服务质量承担责任。“这部法律的最终裁决将在每个尼日利亚人伸手按下开关的地方做出。企业家需要可靠的电力，年轻的尼日利亚人需要就业机会，投资者需要透明的规则，让企业能够繁荣发展。”他补充说。此前，代表电力部长的联邦电力部常任秘书马哈茂达·马曼表示，电力法的成功将取决于各州建立可信机构和商业上可行的电力市场的能力。他指出，州一级的电力规划将使政府能够更有效地响应当地需求和基础设施要求。尼日利亚州长论坛总干事阿卜杜拉蒂夫·O·T·希图博士也在发言中表示，该论坛正致力于加强联邦和州级机构在实施该立法方面的协调。他透露，正在努力为各州制定一个标准电价框架，以保护消费者，同时促进投资和商业可持续性。希图博士敦促利益相关者确保对现有法律框架的任何修订都能加强电力监管方面已经取得的进展。在她的发言中，NERC合规部副总经理兼合规主管豪瓦·雅库布透露，该委员会已向17个州发出监管移交，其中阿夸伊博姆州是最近的一个。她说，委员会通过同行对等培训和技术交流继续支持新成立的州电力监管机构。据她介绍，2023年电力法开启了多层次电力监管的新时代，将监管责任拉近消费者，并允许各州解决自身特有的电力挑战。
