https://leadership.ng/2027-apc-has-what-.title: 2027: APC Has What It Takes To Win In Northern Nigeria- Pate
https://leadership.ng/2027-apc-has-what-.summary: The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate, has expressed confidence that the All Progressives Congress (APC) has what it takes to win in Northern Nigeria, insisting that President Bola Tinubu’s administration has recorded tangible improvements across key sectors.
https://leadership.ng/2027-apc-has-what-.summary_zh: 卫生和社会福利协调部长穆罕默德·阿里·帕特教授表示相信，全进步大会党拥有在尼日利亚北部获胜的实力，他坚持认为博拉·蒂努布总统的政府已在关键领域取得切实改善
https://leadership.ng/2027-apc-has-what-.body: The Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Ali Pate, has expressed confidence that the All Progressives Congress (APC) has what it takes to win in Northern Nigeria, insisting that President Bola Tinubu’s administration has recorded tangible improvements across key sectors. Pate also claimed that 18 of the 19 northern states were aligned with the APC, with Bauchi being the exception, while expressing optimism that the ruling party would secure significant support in the region ahead of the 2027 general elections. The minister made the remarks during an appearance on Arise News Prime Time on Wednesday night, where he dismissed concerns about the APC’s political prospects in the North, describing negative assessments of the party’s standing as a narrow narrative largely driven by social media and elite circles. He said, “It’s a narrative. It’s a very narrow narrative. It’s largely on the social media and among elite circles.” Responding to the interviewer’s reference to a newspaper assessment of the political situation, Pate argued that many ordinary Nigerians in rural communities were unaware of such reports but were beginning to see the impact of the administration’s policies. “I can assure you that the people in many villages in northern Nigeria have not read ThisDay and its report. And the people on the ground have seen and are seeing the giant strides, but also the sacrifices that President Tinubu has led us to do. And they’re beginning to see light at the end of the tunnel,” he said. The minister maintained that the APC could win through grassroots mobilisation and effective organisation at the polling unit, ward and local government levels. “Forget about the narrow narrative. I believe APC has what it takes to work hard at the polling unit, at the ward level, in local government, to get out the votes and win fair and square,” Pate said. Speaking specifically about Bauchi State, he described the APC as the largest political party in the state, claiming that members of the ruling party were defecting to the opposition party. “In Bauchi, for instance, APC is by far the largest party. And every day, including in last 24 hours, you hear the ruling party in the state losing votes from its executive council,” he said. Pate added that a member of the state House of Assembly had informed him of plans to join the APC, while citing a recent by-election victory as evidence of the party’s growing political strength. However, the interviewer challenged the minister’s argument, noting that the concerns of ordinary Nigerians extended beyond political alignments and newspaper assessments to the rising cost of living and the ability of households to afford basic necessities. In response, Pate argued that Nigerians were beginning to experience improvements following the economic difficulties associated with the removal of the fuel subsidy and the devaluation of the naira. “What I’m saying to you is that there are tangible improvements,” he said. He added, “Three years ago, there was all hue and cry, forced removal of subsidies, on devaluation, on food prices. Those facts abated, and folks have begun to see, even on the security issue, it abated compared to where it was.” The minister acknowledged that security challenges had not been completely resolved but credited Tinubu with confronting the situation and pursuing solutions. “Not completely resolved, wasn’t forced by President Bola Ahmed Tinubu, but he took it head-on and has been able to provide solutions,” he said. Pate further defended the administration’s performance by highlighting its interventions in education, healthcare, agriculture and infrastructure, arguing that the policies had produced tangible benefits for Nigerians. He cited the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), which provides financial support to eligible students, alongside healthcare initiatives aimed at expanding access to medical services. “Take NELFUND. Take the hundreds and thousands, more than millions of students and their families, not only who have benefited, but a spooky line of sight that wasn’t there before,” he said. On healthcare, the minister highlighted the government’s efforts to expand access to maternal healthcare, strengthen primary healthcare centres and increase health insurance coverage. “See what he’s done in health. More than 80,000 caesarean sections conducted. See the thousands of primary health care centres revitalised. The seven million additional folks who have had insurance,” he said. He also cited the vaccination of more than 109 million children aged zero to nine in 2025, improvements in maternal mortality data and the establishment of cancer treatment centres in Benin, Enugu and Katsina. According to Pate, the administration’s investments in healthcare infrastructure, education, agriculture and support for small and medium-sized enterprises would strengthen public confidence in the ruling party. He expressed optimism that the APC’s grassroots mobilisation and record in government would translate into electoral support in the North. “We’re confident that President Bola Ahmed Tinubu will be leading the fair and square and the north will back him up because we do know various segments of northern society, not the few, that have particular reasons because they are, of course, angling for power,” he said. Pate acknowledged that political opponents had legitimate ambitions in a democracy but insisted that Tinubu would perform strongly in the region. “But the President, we think, will do very well in the north and will work hard to ensure that he does well,” he added. https://leadership.ng/2027-apc-has-what-.title_zh: 2027年：人民民主党拥有在尼日利亚北部获胜的实力——帕特
https://leadership.ng/2027-apc-has-what-.body_zh: 卫生和社会福利协调部长穆罕默德·阿里·帕特教授表示，他相信全进步大会党（APC）具备在尼日利亚北部获胜的实力，并坚称博拉·蒂努布总统领导的政府已在关键领域取得切实改善。帕特还声称，北部19个州中有18个州与全进步大会党保持一致，只有包奇州例外，同时他对执政党在2027年大选前将在该地区获得大量支持表示乐观。部长是在周三晚间参加Arise News Prime Time节目时发表上述言论的，他驳斥了对全进步大会党在北部政治前景的担忧，将对该党地位的负面评价描述为主要由社交媒体和精英圈子推动的狭隘叙事。他说：“这是一个叙事。这是一个非常狭隘的叙事。它主要存在于社交媒体上和精英圈子里。”在回应采访者提到一份报纸对政治局势的评估时，帕特辩称，许多生活在农村社区的普通尼日利亚人并不了解此类报道，但他们已开始看到政府政策的影响。“我可以向你保证，尼日利亚北部的许多村庄里的人们没有读过ThisDay及其报道。而基层民众已经看到并正在看到总统蒂努布带领我们取得的巨大进步，以及所做的牺牲。他们开始看到隧道尽头的曙光，”他说。部长坚持认为，全进步大会党可以通过基层动员以及在投票站、选区和地方政府层面的有效组织来获胜。“忘记那个狭隘的叙事吧。我相信全进步大会党有能力在投票站、在选区层面、在地方政府努力工作，争取选票并堂堂正正地获胜，”帕特说。在具体谈到包奇州时，他形容全进步大会党是该州最大的政党，并声称执政党成员正在叛逃到反对党。“例如在包奇，全进步大会党是迄今为止最大的政党。而且每天，包括过去24小时内，你都会听到该州执政党从其执行委员会中流失选票，”他说。帕特补充说，州议会的一名议员已告知他计划加入全进步大会党，同时他还援引最近一次补选的胜利作为该党政治实力增强的证据。然而，采访者对部长的论点提出质疑，指出普通尼日利亚人的担忧不仅限于政治阵营和报纸评估，还包括生活成本上升以及家庭支付基本必需品的能力。作为回应，帕特辩称，在取消燃油补贴和奈拉贬值带来的经济困难之后，尼日利亚人正开始感受到改善。“我对你说的是，已经出现切实改善，”他说。他补充道：“三年前，出现了各种强烈抗议，强制取消补贴、货币贬值以及食品价格上涨。这些情况已经缓和，人们已经开始看到，即使在安全问题上，与过去相比也已缓和。”部长承认安全挑战尚未完全解决，但赞扬蒂努布直面这一局面并寻求解决方案。“没有完全解决，这不是由博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努布总统造成的，但他迎头面对，并已能够提供解决方案，”他说。帕特进一步为政府的表现辩护，强调其在教育、医疗、农业和基础设施方面的干预措施，并辩称这些政策已为尼日利亚人带来切实利益。他提到了尼日利亚教育贷款基金（NELFUND），该基金为符合条件的学生提供财政支持，以及旨在扩大医疗服务覆盖面的医疗举措。“以NELFUND为例。看看成千上万、超过数百万的学生及其家庭，不仅已经受益，而且看到了以前不存在的清晰前景，”他说。在医疗方面，部长强调了政府扩大孕产妇医疗服务覆盖面、加强初级保健中心和提高医疗保险覆盖率的努力。“看看他在医疗领域所做的。开展了超过8万例剖腹产手术。看看数千个初级保健中心得到振兴。还有700万额外的人获得了保险，”他说。他还提到了2025年为超过1.09亿名0至9岁儿童接种疫苗、孕产妇死亡率数据的改善以及在贝宁、埃努古和卡齐纳建立癌症治疗中心。根据帕特的说法，政府在医疗基础设施、教育、农业以及对中小型企业的支持方面的投资，将增强公众对执政党的信心。他对全进步大会党的基层动员和执政记录将转化为北部选民支持表示乐观。“我们相信，博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努布总统将堂堂正正地领导，而北部将支持他，因为我们确实了解北部社会的各个阶层，而不是少数人，他们有特别的原因，因为他们当然在谋求权力，”他说。帕特承认，在民主制度中政治对手有合理的抱负，但他坚称蒂努布将在该地区表现强劲。“但我们认为，总统将在北部表现非常出色，并将努力确保他做得好，”他补充道。我们拥有优势。获取实时报道、突发独家新闻和独家视角，直接发送到您的手机。不要满足于过时新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS的WhatsApp，获取24/7更新→

For a student loan scheme to inspire confidence, providing funds is only part of the responsibility.
https://leadership.ng/nelfund-a-student-.summary_zh: 在教育成本不断上升的背景下，尼日利亚教育贷款基金（NELFUND）在博拉·蒂努布总统领导下推出，旨在减轻符合条件的贫困学生在教育经费方面的负担。学生贷款法案于2024年4月3日由蒂努布总统签署成为法律，而申请门户网站于2024年5月24日为其初始试点阶段开放。要让学生贷款计划赢得信任，提供资金只是部分责任。
https://leadership.ng/nelfund-a-student-.body: Against the backdrop of rising education costs, the Nigerian Education Loan Fund (NELFUND), introduced under President Bola Tinubu’s administration, was designed to ease the financial burden on eligible students struggling to fund their education. The student loan legislation was signed into law by President Tinubu on April 3, 2024, while the application portal opened for its initial pilot phase on May 24, 2024. The initiative offered hope to students whose financial circumstances threatened their access to higher education. Yet, for some beneficiaries, experiences involving payment confirmation, application processing and academic records have raised questions about whether the relief comes without complications. Their concerns reveal a dilemma: when a programme intended to make education more accessible becomes associated with uncertainty, students who need financial assistance may begin to see borrowing as a risk rather than an opportunity. For a student loan scheme to inspire confidence, providing funds is only part of the responsibility. Applications must be processed efficiently, institutions must maintain accurate records, payments must be properly reconciled, and complaints must be resolved without unnecessarily disrupting students’ academic progress. Where these processes break down, the consequences can extend beyond financial inconvenience. Students may become uncertain about registration, examination eligibility or the release of their results. Even when the underlying problem is administrative, the uncertainty can weigh heavily on those whose academic progress depends on timely resolution. For Pat Madueke, a student at an undisclosed university, an experience with NELFUND in 200 level was enough to discourage another application and leave a ripple effect. Pat said he applied alongside several departmental colleagues, hoping the loan would ease the burden of paying school fees. Instead, the process proved stressful, and he still had to pay some money despite applying for the scheme. The difficulties, according to Pat, became more worrying when examination results were released. Some students, including him, who had applied for the loan could not find their results alongside those of colleagues whose parents had paid their fees. Now at the 400 level, Pat said he is still rewriting courses taken at the 200 level because their results have not been released alongside those of other students. “I still have one 200-level exam to rewrite because of this issue,” Pat said. For Pat, the consequences were not limited to the uncertainty surrounding the results. Preparing to retake the affected examinations also meant additional expenses, including buying textbooks again and making fresh preparations for the courses. The experience ultimately shaped the student’s decision to avoid NELFUND at the 300-level. Rather than risk a repeat of the earlier difficulties, Pat joined others who took up cooking jobs at events and saved their earnings towards school fees. But the work was irregular, and the student said no such opportunity had come in the current academic year, leaving the 400-level fees unsettled. “Due to the NELFUND scare, I did not register for NELFUND in my 300 level. Honestly, the NELFUND experience has been stressful and discouraging because of what we went through, and I don’t think anyone in my department will apply for it anymore. NELFUND is a big no-no for me,” Pat said. Pat’s account illustrates how an experience in one academic session can influence a student’s financial decisions in subsequent years. However, establishing whether the loan process directly caused the missing results, and identifying where responsibility lies, would require confirmation from the university and NELFUND. Pat’s experience is not the only reason some students are hesitant to apply. For others, the concern is less about a problem they have personally encountered and more about the possibility of becoming trapped between the fund and their institutions if their records or payments are not properly reconciled. Anita Eben, a 300-level student of the University of Abuja, said uncertainty over institutional confirmation was a major concern. “What scares me is what happens when NELFUND says it has approved your application, but your university has not confirmed it. I have seen students run from one office to another trying to resolve issues with their fees. Some become worried about whether they will be allowed to sit their examinations. I cannot risk putting my academics,” Eben said. For Agnes Thomas, a 400-level student at Nasarawa State University, the possibility of payment-related complications raises concerns about the time and energy students could lose resolving administrative issues. “I know students who applied because they could not afford their fees, but later had problems getting their payments confirmed by the school. They spent time trying to sort out the issue instead of concentrating on their studies. Even if the loan is meant to help, I am afraid that a problem with confirmation could delay my registration or affect my academic activities,” Thomas said. The concern is not simply whether a loan will be approved, but what happens after approval if the institution’s records do not reflect the expected payment. Sa’adat Ahmed, a sociology student at the Federal University of Lokoja, said the uncertainty over which party would take responsibility in such circumstances was enough to make the student consider other ways of raising school fees. “If NELFUND says it has paid and the university says it has not received or confirmed the money, who takes responsibility? I may not know which office to approach or how long it will take to resolve the issue. I would rather find another way to pay my fees than have my studies suffer because of a problem I cannot control,” Ahmed said. For students in this position, avoiding the loan does not necessarily mean they can comfortably afford their fees. It may simply reflect their preference for a financial difficulty they understand over a process whose potential complications they fear they cannot control. That presents a challenge for a scheme intended to expand access to higher education: the students who most need financial assistance may be among those most reluctant to seek it if they lack confidence in how problems will be handled. While some students are steering clear of NELFUND, a controversy at the Enugu State College of Education (Technical), Enugu, raised a different question: what happens when students who would rather not borrow are directed to apply for the loan? An internal memorandum dated October 6, 2026, and signed by the college’s Registrar, Patrick A. Aneke, directed fresh and returning students in its Nigeria Certificate in Education (NCE) and degree programmes to enrol for and access NELFUND for the 2026/2027 academic session. The memo instructed students to visit the college’s NELFUND Desk Officer, Dr Rufina Agu, for assistance with their applications. It also directed deans, directors, heads of academic departments and the Student Union Government to communicate the directive to students. The controversy intensified following reports that students who failed to comply could encounter difficulties obtaining examination clearance. The memo was reported to require evidence of NELFUND registration before students could sit their examinations. The directive appeared to place students in a difficult position, particularly those whose families preferred to pay their fees directly or who had reservations about taking on a loan. NELFUND subsequently clarified that participation in the scheme was voluntary, not compulsory. According to the fund, compelling students who do not need financial assistance to take loans would defeat the programme’s purpose. “The objective is not to encourage every student to borrow, but to ensure that every eligible Nigerian student who genuinely needs financial assistance has the opportunity to access it,” NELFUND said. The clarification underscores the distinction between making financial assistance available and requiring students to take it. While institutions have a responsibility to inform eligible students about funding opportunities, the fund’s position is that students should not be compelled to borrow. The episode also raises questions about how institutions communicate loan requirements, distinguish registration from actual borrowing, and ensure that administrative directives do not undermine students’ ability to make informed financial decisions. Beyond the immediate concerns over applications and payments, the experiences described by students point to the need for clearer accountability among NELFUND, participating institutions and beneficiaries. Speaking with LEADERSHIP, lawyer and analyst Hassan Dotun said universities and colleges must maintain accurate student records, verify applications and reconcile payments. “Students need accessible channels through which they can report discrepancies and obtain explanations when problems occur. When incomplete or inaccurate institutional documentation contributes to a problem, students should not be left uncertain about their academic status while the relevant parties resolve the issue. “However, responsibility must be established through evidence rather than assumed from a student’s experience alone,” he said. Dotun said NELFUND also needed to clarify the respective responsibilities of the fund and participating institutions, explain how beneficiaries could escalate complaints, and ensure that students understood the steps to take when discrepancies arose. “Universities and colleges, in turn, need to communicate clearly about fee payments, examination eligibility and the handling of loan beneficiaries’ academic records. Students who are uncertain about repayment obligations also need accessible explanations of the loan terms before deciding whether to apply,” he added. The challenge, therefore, extends beyond encouraging students to use the scheme. Confidence will depend on whether the process is transparent, whether payment and academic records are properly reconciled, and whether students can obtain timely answers when something goes wrong. https://leadership.ng/nelfund-a-student-.body_zh: 在教育成本不断上升的背景下，尼日利亚教育贷款基金（NELFUND）由博拉·蒂努布总统领导的政府推出，旨在减轻符合条件的贫困学生在教育经费方面的负担。该学生贷款法案于2024年4月3日由蒂努布总统签署成为法律，而申请门户于2024年5月24日为其初始试点阶段开放。这一举措为那些财务状况威胁到接受高等教育机会的学生带来了希望。然而，对一些受益者而言，涉及付款确认、申请处理和学术记录的经历引发了疑问，即这种救济是否毫无 complications。他们的担忧揭示了一个困境：当一个旨在让教育更易获得的计划与不确定性联系在一起时，需要财务援助的学生可能会开始将借贷视为风险而非机会。要让学生贷款计划激发信心，提供资金只是部分责任。申请必须高效处理，院校必须保持准确记录，付款必须妥善核对，投诉必须得到解决而不会不必要地干扰学生的学业进展。如果这些流程出现故障，后果可能超出财务不便。学生可能会对注册、考试资格或成绩发布感到不确定。即使根本问题是行政性的，这种不确定性也会对那些学业进展依赖及时解决的学生造成沉重压力。对帕特·马杜埃克来说，一名在未公开大学的就读学生，在200级时与NELFUND打交道的经历足以让他放弃再次申请并产生连锁效应。帕特说他与几名系里的同学一起申请，希望贷款能减轻缴纳学费的负担。相反，这个过程证明充满压力，而且尽管申请了该计划，他仍然不得不支付部分费用。据帕特说，当考试成绩公布时，这些困难变得更加令人担忧。一些申请了贷款的学生，包括他在内，无法与那些父母已支付学费的同学一起找到自己的成绩。现在读到400级，帕特说他仍在重修200级时修过的课程，因为他们的成绩没有与其他学生一起发布。“由于这个问题，我还有一门200级的考试需要重考，”帕特说。对帕特来说，后果不仅限于围绕成绩的不确定性。准备重考受影响的考试也意味着额外开支，包括再次购买教科书并为课程做新的准备。这一经历最终影响了该学生在300级时避开NELFUND的决定。为了避免重复先前的困难，帕特加入了其他在活动上做烹饪工作并将收入存起来支付学费的学生行列。但工作不稳定，该学生说在本学年没有这样的机会，导致400级的费用仍未解决。“由于NELFUND的可怕经历，我在300级时没有注册NELFUND。老实说，NELFUND的经历一直充满压力和令人沮丧，因为我们所经历的事情，我认为我们系里不会再有人申请它了。对我来说NELFUND是绝对不行的，”帕特说。帕特的叙述说明了一个学期的经历如何影响学生在随后几年的财务决定。然而，要确定贷款流程是否直接导致成绩缺失，并找出责任所在，需要大学和NELFUND的确认。帕特的经历并不是一些学生犹豫申请的唯一原因。对其他人来说，担忧与其说是他们个人遇到的问题，不如说是如果记录或付款没有得到妥善核对，他们可能会被困在基金和院校之间。阿尼塔·埃本，阿布贾大学的一名300级学生，说对院校确认的不确定性是一个主要担忧。“让我害怕的是，当NELFUND说它已批准你的申请，但你的大学没有确认时会发生什么。我见过学生从一个办公室跑到另一个办公室试图解决费用问题。有些人担心他们是否会被允许参加考试。我不能冒险影响我的学业，”埃本说。对阿格尼丝·托马斯，纳萨拉瓦州立大学的一名400级学生来说，与付款相关的潜在 complications 引发了对学生可能在解决行政问题上损失时间和精力的担忧。“我知道有些学生因为付不起学费而申请，但后来在让学校确认付款时遇到问题。他们花时间试图解决问题而不是专注于学业。即使贷款旨在提供帮助，我担心确认问题可能会延迟我的注册或影响我的学术活动，”托马斯说。担忧不仅仅是贷款是否会被批准，而是批准后如果院校记录没有反映预期付款会发生什么。萨阿达特·艾哈迈德，洛科贾联邦大学的一名社会学学生，说在这种情况下对哪一方承担责任的不确定性足以让学生考虑其他筹集学费的方式。“如果NELFUND说它已支付而大学说它没有收到或确认这笔钱，谁来承担责任？我可能不知道该找哪个办公室或需要多长时间来解决问题。我宁愿找另一种方式支付学费，也不愿让我的学业因为我无法控制的问题而受损，”艾哈迈德说。对处于这种位置的学生来说，避免贷款并不一定意味着他们能轻松负担学费。它可能只是反映出他们更喜欢自己能理解的财务困难，而不是害怕自己无法控制其潜在 complications 的过程。这对一个旨在扩大高等教育机会的计划提出了挑战：最需要财务援助的学生如果对问题如何处理缺乏信心，可能会是最不愿寻求帮助的人之一。虽然一些学生避开NELFUND，但恩古古州教育学院（技术）的争议提出了一个不同的问题：当宁愿不借贷的学生被指示申请贷款时会发生什么？一份日期为2026年10月6日的内部备忘录，由学院注册官帕特里克·A·阿内克签署，指示其尼日利亚教育证书（NCE）和学位课程的新生和返校学生为2026/2027学年注册并获取NELFUND。该备忘录指示学生访问学院的NELFUND服务台官员鲁菲娜·阿古博士以获得申请协助。它还指示院长、主任、学术系主任和学生会政府将该指示传达给学生。在有报告称未遵守的学生可能在获得考试许可时遇到困难后，争议加剧了。据报道，该备忘录要求在学生参加考试前提供NELFUND注册证明。该指示似乎将学生置于困难境地，特别是那些家庭更愿意直接支付学费或对承担贷款有保留意见的学生。NELFUND随后澄清，参与该计划是自愿的，而非强制性的。根据该基金，强迫不需要财务援助的学生接受贷款将违背该计划的目的。“目标不是鼓励每个学生借贷，而是确保每个真正需要财务援助的符合条件的尼日利亚学生有机会获得它，”NELFUND说。这一澄清强调了提供财务援助与要求学生接受它之间的区别。虽然院校有责任告知符合条件的学生可用的资助机会，但该基金的立场是学生不应被强迫借贷。这一事件还引发了关于院校如何传达贷款要求、区分注册与实际借贷以及确保行政指示不会削弱学生做出知情财务决定的能力的问题。除了对申请和付款的直接担忧外，学生描述的经历指向NELFUND、参与院校和受益者之间需要更明确的问责制。在与LEADERSHIP的交谈中，律师和分析师哈桑·多顿说，大学和学院必须保持准确的学生记录、验证申请并核对付款。“学生需要可访问的渠道，通过这些渠道他们可以报告差异并在问题发生时获得解释。当不完整或不准确的院校文件导致问题时，学生不应在相关各方解决问题期间对其学术地位感到不确定。“然而，责任必须通过证据来确立，而不是仅仅从学生的经历中假设，”他说。多顿说NELFUND还需要澄清基金和参与院校各自的责任，解释受益者如何升级投诉，并确保学生了解差异出现时应采取的步骤。“反过来，大学和学院需要清楚地沟通关于费用支付、考试资格以及贷款受益者学术记录的处理。对还款义务不确定的学生在决定是否申请前也需要对贷款条款的可访问解释，”他补充说。因此，这一挑战超出了鼓励学生使用该计划的范围。信心将取决于流程是否透明、付款和学术记录是否得到妥善核对，以及当出现问题时学生是否能及时获得答案。我们拥有优势。获取实时报道、突发独家新闻和独家角度，直接发送到您的手机。不要满足于陈旧新闻。加入LEADERSHIP https://leadership.ng/presidency-expands.summary: Both presidential aides recognised the need for a comprehensive security approach combining military and law enforcement operations with education, skills development and economic inclusion, particularly for vulnerable youths. Famadewa stressed the need for a holistic approach to insecurity that incorporates non-kinetic measures and addresses its underlying socioeconomic drivers.
https://leadership.ng/presidency-expands.summary_zh: 两位总统助手都认识到需要采取全面的安全方法，将军事和执法行动与教育、技能发展和经济包容结合起来，特别是针对弱势青年。法马德瓦强调需要采取整体方法应对不安全问题，纳入非军事手段并解决其潜在的社会经济驱动因素。
https://leadership.ng/presidency-expands.body: Senior Special Assistant to President Bola Tinubu on Technical, Vocational and Entrepreneurship Education (TVEE), Dr Abiola Arogundade disclosed this on Wednesday in Abuja during a meeting with Maj.-Gen. Adeyinka A. Famadewa (Rtd), Special Adviser to the President on Homeland Security, at her office. The meeting explored areas of collaboration between the two offices, focusing on economic empowerment, employability and sustainable livelihoods as complementary measures to conventional security operations. Arogundade said the partnership seeks to empower citizens, expand awareness and create sustainable opportunities for positive engagement. “This partnership seeks to strengthen cooperation between both offices in empowering our people, broadening their awareness, and creating sustainable opportunities for their positive engagement. “Through these collective efforts, we aim to steer them away from crime and criminality while fostering a safer, more enlightened, and empowered society,” she said. Both presidential aides recognised the need for a comprehensive security approach combining military and law enforcement operations with education, skills development and economic inclusion, particularly for vulnerable youths. Under the proposed collaboration, the TVEE would seek to reduce the vulnerability of unemployed and economically disadvantaged youths to recruitment by criminal networks exploiting poverty, limited opportunities and social exclusion. By linking vocational education with homeland security objectives, the partnership is expected to strengthen community resilience, promote social stability and support individuals seeking alternatives to criminal activities. Famadewa stressed the need for a holistic approach to insecurity that incorporates non-kinetic measures and addresses its underlying socioeconomic drivers. His office is also focused on unified intelligence and surveillance, stronger border security, improved identification of security threats, and effective protocols for reporting and responding to crises. The proposed collaboration reflects President Bola Ahmed Tinubu’s administration’s efforts to link education, economic opportunities, and national security. By promoting skills development and supporting entrepreneurship, the initiative aims to create pathways to sustainable livelihoods, strengthen peacebuilding efforts and foster long-term stability. https://leadership.ng/presidency-expands.title_zh: 总统府扩大技能培训计划以应对不安全问题
https://leadership.ng/presidency-expands.body_zh: 总统博拉·蒂努布负责技术和职业教育与创业教育（TVEE）的高级特别助理阿比奥拉·阿罗贡达德博士于周三在阿布贾她的办公室与总统国土安全特别顾问、退役少将阿德因卡·A·法马德瓦举行会晤时披露了这一信息。会晤探讨了两个办公室之间的合作领域，重点关注经济赋权、就业能力和可持续生计，将其作为常规安全行动的补充措施。阿罗贡达德表示，这一伙伴关系旨在赋权公民、扩大意识并为积极参与创造可持续机会。“这一伙伴关系旨在加强两个办公室之间的合作，以赋权我们的民众、拓宽他们的意识，并为他们的积极参与创造可持续机会。”“通过这些集体努力，我们旨在引导他们远离犯罪和违法行为，同时培育一个更安全、更开明和更有力量的社会，”她说。两位总统助理都认识到需要采取全面的安全方法，将军事和执法行动与教育、技能发展和经济包容结合起来，尤其是针对弱势青年。在拟议的合作下，技术和职业教育与创业教育办公室将寻求减少失业和经济弱势青年被犯罪网络招募的脆弱性，这些犯罪网络利用贫困、机会有限和社会排斥。通过将职业教育与国土安全目标联系起来，这一伙伴关系有望加强社区韧性、促进社会稳定并支持寻求犯罪活动替代方案的个人。法马德瓦强调需要对不安全问题采取整体方法，纳入非军事手段并解决其潜在的社会经济驱动因素。他的办公室还专注于统一情报和监视、更强的边境安全、更好地识别安全威胁以及报告和应对危机的有效协议。这一拟议的合作反映了博拉·艾哈迈德·蒂努布总统政府将教育、经济机会和国家安全联系起来的努力。通过促进技能发展和支持创业，该举措旨在创造通往可持续生计的途径，加强和平建设努力并促进长期稳定。我们拥有优势。获取实时报道、突发独家新闻和独家视角，直接发送到您的手机。不要满足于陈旧新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS的WhatsApp，获取24/7更新→

https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.title: Reps demand review of Lagos-Calabar coastal highway realignment
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.summary: The House of Representatives has urged the federal government to retain the originally conceptualised alignment of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway through Ondo State and the Escravos–Ogheye–Ugborodo corridor in Delta State, calling for a review of the proposed realignment. The Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is a major federal road project designed to connect communities and economic centres along Nigeria’s Atlantic coastline, from Lagos to Calabar in Cross River State.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.summary_zh: 众议院敦促联邦政府保留拉各斯-卡拉巴尔沿海公路最初设想的路线，即途经翁多州以及三角洲州的埃斯克拉沃斯-奥盖耶-乌博罗多走廊，并要求审查拟议的改线方案。拉各斯-卡拉巴尔沿海公路是一项重要的联邦道路项目，旨在连接尼日利亚大西洋沿岸从拉各斯到克罗斯河州卡拉巴尔的社区和经济中心。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.body: The House of Representatives has urged the federal government to retain the originally conceptualised alignment of the Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway through Ondo State and the Escravos–Ogheye–Ugborodo corridor in Delta State, calling for a review of the proposed realignment. The lawmakers warned that diverting the highway away from coastal communities could undermine the project’s original objectives of improving connectivity, facilitating trade and unlocking economic opportunities in the region. The motion was moved by Thomas Ereyitomi (APC, Delta) during Wednesday’s plenary. The lawmaker raised concerns about the proposed route bypassing riverine communities in Delta State, including the Ogheye, Orere, Ugborodo, and Escravos corridor, where major oil and gas infrastructure is located. The Lagos-Calabar Coastal Highway is a major federal road project designed to connect communities and economic centres along Nigeria’s Atlantic coastline, from Lagos to Calabar in Cross River State. The project was initially conceived as a roughly 700-kilometre corridor and is intended to improve movement, trade and access to coastal communities across several states. The federal government has recently defended changes being considered for sections of the route, citing difficult terrain, flooding, weak subsoil conditions and climate-related risks. Minister of Works Dave Umahi said the government intends to use portions of the existing East-West Road in the affected corridor, while maintaining the wider coastal highway project. However, the House said any change to the route should be subjected to an independent assessment of its engineering requirements, environmental consequences, socioeconomic impact and total lifecycle cost. Mr Ereyitomi said the proposed realignment could prevent coastal communities from benefiting from a project specifically conceived to improve connectivity along the coastline. “The proposed realignments may compromise the project’s original connectivity and economic-development objectives if their comparative engineering requirements, environmental consequences, socioeconomic implications, and total lifecycle costs are not independently assessed,” he said. He noted that retaining the original coastal alignment would improve access to communities and economic hubs hosting oil and gas infrastructure, including the Chevron tank farm and Escravos Gas-to-Liquids plant. He also said the route would improve the movement of workers, equipment, and commercial goods while creating opportunities to connect roads and other infrastructure in coastal areas. He urged the federal government to consider the full cost of alternative routes, including additional road distance, bridges, ground improvement, environmental mitigation, compensation, flood protection and long-term maintenance. Mr Ereyitomi also suggested that engineering solutions such as soil stabilisation, geosynthetics, piled foundations, reinforced embankments and elevated viaducts could be considered where technically and environmentally appropriate. Contributing to the debate, Inombek Abiante, a Rivers lawmaker, questioned the justification for moving the road away from coastal communities. Mr Abiante said the communities had long suffered from poor infrastructure despite the economic value of the resources extracted from their areas. “If crude oil were found in those areas, would they say the terrain was difficult?” He questioned whether the government would have accepted difficult terrain as a reason to abandon the area if the purpose was to extract crude oil. Mr Abiante also demanded that the expert proposing the realignment should appear before the House to explain the technical reasons for the change. “I want to know why he wants to deny me the little benefit I stand to gain after this government and this country have exploited my people and me to the point of exhaustion,” he said. He also said no environmental impact assessment of the project had been made available to his constituency. Mr Abiante initially questioned whether the House Committee on Works could adequately protect his interests, prompting Speaker Abbas Tajudeen to ask him to withdraw the statement. Mr Tajudeen said lawmakers should show confidence in House committees but agreed the committee could be directed to do further work on the issue. Mr Abiante later clarified that he wanted the committee to consider the interests of affected communities and also called for an interface with the Works Minister. He said coastal communities needed to understand why the realignment was being proposed so lawmakers could give their constituents accurate information. “We do not want the road to be realigned elsewhere. God has remembered us through Mr President,” he said. He recalled that it took almost 50 years for a road to reach Bonny, even though crude oil was first shipped from the area in 1965. Mark Esset (APC, Akwa Ibom), in an amendment to the motion, asked the Federal Ministry of Works to submit the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) for the highway to the House through the relevant committee. Mr Esset said making the assessment available would help lawmakers understand the project’s environmental challenges and the measures proposed to address them. He argued that the assessment should have been completed and considered before construction work began. “If that had been done, Mr Speaker, I do not think we would have found ourselves in this situation today,” he said. He said the EIA would help identify potential environmental challenges and the measures required to mitigate them. Ademorin Kuye, a Lagos lawmaker, proposed that the Federal Ministry of Works review the proposed realignment while providing alternative access for communities that could be cut off by the change. He said that where the main dual carriageway had to move inland because of deep water pits and unstable terrain, reinforced coastal feeder roads should be built to reconnect maritime and fishing communities to the main highway. Mr Kuye also called for relevant business proponents to explain the reasons for the realignment and for alternative access routes to be designed to minimise displacement. He further proposed attaching a timeline to the implementation of the measures. After debate, the lawmakers adopted the motion when it was put to a vote by Mr Tajudeen
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.title_zh: 众议员要求审查拉各斯-卡拉巴尔沿海公路重新调整路线
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/regional/.body_zh: 众议院敦促联邦政府保留原先构想的拉各斯-卡拉巴尔沿海公路穿越翁多州的路线以及三角洲州埃斯克拉沃斯-奥赫耶-乌博罗多走廊，并要求对拟议的改线方案进行审查。议员们警告称，将公路从沿海社区改道可能削弱该项目原本旨在改善连通性、促进贸易并释放该地区经济机会的目标。该动议由托马斯·埃雷伊托米（APC，三角洲州）在周三全体会议期间提出。这位议员对拟议路线绕过三角洲州河流社区表示担忧，这些社区包括奥赫耶、奥雷雷、乌博罗多和埃斯克拉沃斯走廊，那里分布着主要的石油和天然气基础设施。拉各斯-卡拉巴尔沿海公路是一项重要的联邦道路项目，旨在连接尼日利亚大西洋沿岸从拉各斯到克罗斯河州卡拉巴尔的社区和经济中心。该项目最初构想为约700公里长的走廊，旨在改善多个州的交通、贸易和沿海社区的通达性。联邦政府最近为考虑对部分路段进行的改动进行辩护，理由是地形困难、洪水、土壤条件薄弱以及气候相关风险。工程部长戴夫·乌马希表示，政府打算在受影响走廊使用部分现有的东西向公路，同时维持更广泛的沿海公路项目。然而，众议院表示，任何路线变更都应接受对其工程要求、环境后果、社会经济影响和全生命周期成本的独立评估。埃雷伊托米先生说，拟议的改线可能使沿海社区无法从专门为改善海岸线连通性而构想的项目中受益。他说：“如果不对拟议改线的工程要求、环境后果、社会经济影响和全生命周期成本进行独立评估，这些改线可能损害项目的原始连通性和经济发展目标。”他指出，保留原沿海路线将改善对拥有石油和天然气基础设施的社区和经济枢纽的通达性，包括雪佛龙储油场和埃斯克拉沃斯天然气制液体工厂。他还表示，该路线将改善工人、设备和商业货物的运输，同时创造机会连接沿海地区的道路和其他基础设施。他敦促联邦政府考虑替代路线的全部成本，包括额外道路距离、桥梁、地基加固、环境缓解、补偿、洪水防护和长期维护。埃雷伊托米先生还建议，在技术和环境适当的情况下，可以考虑土壤稳定、土工合成材料、桩基、加固路堤和高架桥等工程解决方案。在辩论中，河流州议员伊诺姆贝克·阿比安特质疑将道路从沿海社区移走的理由。阿比安特先生说，尽管这些社区的资源被开采具有经济价值，但它们长期以来一直遭受基础设施落后的困扰。他说：“如果那些地区发现了原油，他们还会说地形困难吗？”他质疑，如果目的是开采原油，政府是否会接受地形困难作为放弃该地区的理由。阿比安特先生还要求提出改线方案的专家到众议院说明变更的技术原因。他说：“我想知道他为什么要剥夺我在这个政府和这个国家把我和我的族人剥削到筋疲力尽之后本应获得的那一点点利益。”他还表示，该项目的环境影响评估从未向他的选区提供。阿比安特先生最初质疑众议院工程委员会是否能充分保护他的利益，这促使议长阿巴斯·塔朱丁要求他撤回该言论。塔朱丁先生说，议员们应对众议院委员会表现出信心，但他同意可以指示该委员会就此问题做进一步工作。阿比安特先生后来澄清说，他希望委员会考虑受影响社区的利益，并呼吁与工程部长进行沟通。他说，沿海社区需要了解为什么提出改线方案，以便议员们能向选民提供准确信息。他说：“我们不希望道路改到其他地方。上帝通过总统先生记起了我们。”他回忆说，尽管该地区1965年就开始出口原油，但花了近50年时间才有一条公路通到博尼。马克·埃塞特（APC，阿夸伊博姆州）在对动议的修正案中，要求联邦工程部通过相关委员会向众议院提交该公路的环境影响评估（EIA）。埃塞特先生说，提供该评估将帮助议员们了解项目的环境挑战以及拟议的应对措施。他说，该评估本应在施工开始前完成并审议。他说：“议长先生，如果当时这样做了，我认为我们今天就不会陷入这种局面。”他说，环境影响评估将有助于识别潜在的环境挑战以及缓解这些挑战所需的措施。拉各斯州议员阿德莫林·库耶提议，联邦工程部在审查拟议改线方案的同时，为可能因变更而被切断的社区提供替代通道。他说，如果主双车道公路因深水坑和不稳定地形必须向内陆移动，则应修建加固的沿海支线道路，将海事和渔业社区重新连接到主公路。库耶先生还呼吁相关业务提议者解释改线的原因，并设计替代通道以尽量减少搬迁。他进一步提议为这些措施的实施附上时间表。辩论结束后，议员们在塔朱丁先生付诸表决时通过了该动议。

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/80m-.body: Layer 1 The Federal Government says an estimated 80 million children in Nigeria are exposed to lead poisoning, calling for stronger measures to address the public health and environmental threat. Salako said children, women of childbearing age and pregnant women were particularly vulnerable to lead exposure, which could cause serious and lasting health consequences. “It is a toxic substance capable of affecting multiple body systems, with children, women of childbearing age and pregnant women being particularly vulnerable. “Exposure can have serious and lasting consequences, while individuals may be exposed without immediate obvious symptoms. This makes prevention, early identification and timely action essential components of any national response,” he added. The minister said the government had established an Inter-Agency Working Group on Lead Poisoning Prevention and Elimination to coordinate efforts involving relevant Ministries, Departments and Agencies, development partners and other stakeholders. Salako said experiences in Lagos, Ogun, Sokoto and Zamfara had highlighted different sources of exposure and the need for state-specific interventions. He cited environmental investigations in Lagos and lead exposure concerns associated with battery recycling in Ogijo, Ogun, as evidence of the need for stronger environmental and occupational controls. “We cannot treat our way out of lead poisoning; we must prevent exposure wherever possible,” the minister said. While inaugurating the Five-Year Strategic Plan on Lead Poisoning Elimination in Nigeria (2026–2030), Salako added that a costed three-year national roadmap was being developed to translate the plan’s priorities into time-bound actions. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the plan is aimed at guiding stakeholders on coordinated efforts to prevent exposure, strengthen surveillance and address environmental and occupational sources. The minister identified stronger monitoring of soil, dust, water, industrial emissions and consumer products, alongside improved regulation, enforcement and laboratory capacity, as priorities. He urged states, particularly Lagos, Ogun, Zamfara and Sokoto, to develop prevention and control action plans, and called for community involvement in identifying exposure risks. He called on all stakeholders to eliminate exposure sources like lead-based paint dust, contaminated soil, unsafe work practices and unsafe water pipes. He also cautioned against lead-glazed pottery, toys, cosmetics including traditional eyeliners (tiro) and some traditional remedies. The minister listed preventive measures to include wearing protective clothing when handling items containing lead during construction, painting and recycling. He said others included daily preventive habits like handwashing, washing children’s toys, and wet-wiping floors and play areas instead of dry sweeping. “Keeping children and pregnant women away from areas where lead may be released, such as battery recycling, repair or painting areas. “Eating nutrient-dense foods high in calcium, iron and Vitamin C, which block the body from absorbing lead,” he said. Dr Sarah Ango, a UNICEF consultant, described lead poisoning as a preventable but often invisible threat to children’s health and development. She said UNICEF was committed to ending childhood lead poisoning by 2040 and was supporting government efforts to strengthen surveillance, laboratory capacity, risk communication and policy implementation. Ango emphasised that there was no safe level of lead exposure for children. “This year’s commemoration, under the theme From Detection to Prevention, provides an opportunity to move beyond identifying the problem to accelerating practical solutions that address the root causes of lead exposure,” she said. The Principal Adviser, Resolve to Save Lives, Mrs Okeoma Obasi, said the organisation had supported surveillance systems, laboratory testing capacity, evidence generation and public awareness. She described prevention as the most effective and cost-effective strategy for protecting children from lead poisoning. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the International Lead Poisoning Prevention Week, observed from Oct. 18 to Oct. 24, is aimed at raising awareness on lead exposure and promoting measures to eliminate it. https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/80m-.title_zh: 8000万尼日利亚儿童面临铅中毒风险
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/80m-.body_zh: 第一层 联邦政府表示，尼日利亚约有8000万儿童面临铅中毒风险，并呼吁采取更有力措施来应对这一公共卫生和环境威胁。萨拉科说，儿童、育龄妇女和孕妇特别容易受到铅暴露的影响，这可能导致严重且持久的健康后果。“这是一种有毒物质，能够影响多个身体系统，其中儿童、育龄妇女和孕妇特别容易受到影响。暴露可能产生严重且持久的后果，而个人可能在没有立即明显症状的情况下接触到铅。这使得预防、早期识别和及时行动成为任何国家应对措施的基本组成部分，”他补充说。部长表示，政府已成立了一个铅中毒预防和消除跨部门工作组，以协调涉及相关部委、部门和机构、发展伙伴及其他利益攸关方的努力。萨拉科说，拉各斯、奥贡、索科托和扎姆法拉的经验凸显了不同的暴露来源以及需要采取州别干预措施的必要性。他引用在拉各斯进行的环境调查以及与奥贡州奥吉乔电池回收相关的铅暴露担忧，作为需要加强环境和职业控制的证据。“我们不能仅靠治疗来摆脱铅中毒；我们必须尽可能防止暴露，”部长说。在启动《尼日利亚消除铅中毒五年战略计划（2026-2030年）》时，萨拉科补充说，正在制定一份成本核算的三年国家路线图，以将该计划的优先事项转化为有时限的行动。尼日利亚通讯社报道称，该计划旨在指导利益攸关方开展协调努力，以防止暴露、加强监测并解决环境和职业来源问题。部长将加强对土壤、灰尘、水、工业排放和消费产品的监测，以及改善监管、执法和实验室能力列为优先事项。他敦促各州，特别是拉各斯、奥贡、扎姆法拉和索科托，制定预防和控制行动计划，并呼吁社区参与识别暴露风险。他呼吁所有利益攸关方消除铅基涂料粉尘、受污染土壤、不安全工作做法和不安全水管等暴露来源。他还警告不要使用铅釉陶器、玩具、化妆品包括传统眼线膏（tiro）和一些传统药物。部长列出的预防措施包括在建筑、涂漆和回收过程中处理含铅物品时穿戴防护服。他说其他措施包括日常预防习惯，如洗手、清洗儿童玩具，以及用湿布擦拭地板和游戏区而不是干扫。“让儿童和孕妇远离可能释放铅的区域，如电池回收、修理或涂漆区域。食用富含钙、铁和维生素C的营养密集食物，这些食物能阻止身体吸收铅，”他说。联合国儿童基金会顾问萨拉·安戈博士将铅中毒描述为对儿童健康和发展的一种可预防但往往隐形的威胁。她说，联合国儿童基金会致力于到2040年结束儿童铅中毒，并正在支持政府加强监测、实验室能力、风险沟通和政策实施的努力。安戈强调，对儿童来说不存在安全的铅暴露水平。“今年纪念活动的主题是‘从检测到预防’，提供了一个机会，让我们超越识别问题，转而加快解决铅暴露根源的实际解决方案，”她说。决心拯救生命组织的首席顾问奥克奥马·奥巴西夫人表示，该组织支持了监测系统、实验室检测能力、证据生成和公众意识。她将预防描述为保护儿童免受铅中毒的最有效和最具成本效益的策略。尼日利亚通讯社报道称，国际铅中毒预防周于10月18日至10月24日举行，旨在提高对铅暴露的认识并促进消除铅暴露的措施。此处表达的评论不反映先锋报或其任何员工的意见

The companies, including MTN Nigeria, Airtel Nigeria, Globacom (Glo) and Mafab Communications Ltd., are expected to appear before the House Ad Hoc Committee investigating the poor quality of telecommunications services on 28 October.
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.summary_zh: 众议院已要求主要电信公司的首席执行官在七天内到场，解释尼日利亚各地网络服务持续恶化的问题。这些公司包括MTN Nigeria、Airtel Nigeria、Globacom（Glo）和Mafab Communications Ltd.，预计将在10月28日出席众议院特设委员会，就电信服务质量差的问题接受调查。
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body: The House of Representatives has given the chief executive officers of major telecommunications companies seven days to appear before it and explain the persistent deterioration in network services across Nigeria. The companies, including MTN Nigeria, Airtel Nigeria, Globacom (Glo) and Mafab Communications Ltd., are expected to appear before the House Ad Hoc Committee investigating the poor quality of telecommunications services on 28 October. The committee issued the ultimatum at a public hearing in Abuja on Wednesday after several invited operators failed to appear. The committee directed the Nigerian Communications Commission (NCC) to ensure that all affected telecommunications operators comply with the invitation and appear at 2 p.m. on 28 October in Hearing Room 447 of the New Building of the National Assembly Complex, Abuja. The committee warned that chief executives who fail to honour the invitation could be summoned to appear. Chairman of the committee, Olumide Osoba (APC, Ogun), said reliable telecommunications services had become essential to Nigeria’s economy, with their importance extending beyond calls and internet access. He cited businesses, financial transactions, and Point of Sale (POS) operations as activities that depend heavily on telecommunications networks. He expressed concern that some of the invited companies had avoided direct engagement with the committee by sending junior officials or offering excuses for the absence of their chief executives. According to him, the committee expects the CEOs to appear personally because they are in a position to explain the operational challenges facing their companies and the measures being taken to address them. Another committee member, Ibe Osonwa (LP, Abia), also criticised the operators for failing to honour the invitation. Mr Osonwa said it was unacceptable for companies generating substantial revenue from the Nigerian market to disregard an invitation from the legislature, particularly when the inquiry concerned services affecting millions of their customers. He said the operators must be held accountable for the quality of services they provide and warned that the House would not allow attempts to frustrate its investigation. Mr Osoba subsequently directed the NCC to ensure compliance with the committee’s resolution and reiterated that the affected telecommunications companies must appear before the lawmakers on 28 October with the requested documents and explanations
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.title_zh: 众议员传唤MTN、Airtel、Glo首席执行官，讨论网络质量差问题
https://www.premiumtimesng.com/news/top-.body_zh: 众议院已要求主要电信公司首席执行官在七天内到场，解释尼日利亚全国网络服务持续恶化的问题。这些公司包括MTN尼日利亚、Airtel尼日利亚、Globacom（Glo）和Mafab Communications Ltd.，预计将于10月28日出席众议院特设委员会就电信服务质量低劣问题进行的调查。该委员会于周三在阿布贾举行公开听证会后发出最后通牒，此前多名受邀运营商未能到场。委员会指示尼日利亚通信委员会（NCC）确保所有受影响的电信运营商遵守邀请，于10月28日下午2点在阿布贾国民议会综合大楼新楼447号听证室出席。委员会警告称，未能遵守邀请的首席执行官可能会被传唤到场。委员会主席奥卢米德·奥索巴（APC，奥贡州）表示，可靠的电信服务已成为尼日利亚经济不可或缺的部分，其重要性远超通话和互联网接入。他列举了企业、金融交易以及销售点（POS）业务等高度依赖电信网络的活动。他对一些受邀公司通过派初级官员出席或为首席执行官缺席找借口来回避与委员会直接接触表示担忧。据他介绍，委员会希望首席执行官亲自出席，因为他们有能力解释公司面临的运营挑战以及正在采取的解决措施。另一名委员会成员伊贝·奥索恩瓦（LP，阿比亚州）也批评运营商未能遵守邀请。奥索恩瓦先生表示，这些从尼日利亚市场获得大量收入的公司无视立法机构的邀请是不可接受的，尤其是调查涉及影响数百万客户的服务时。他说，必须追究运营商提供服务质量的责任，并警告众议院不会允许任何阻挠调查的企图。奥索巴先生随后指示尼日利亚通信委员会确保遵守委员会决议，并重申受影响的电信公司必须于10月28日携带所要求的文件和解释材料到议员面前出席。

https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/no-e.body: The Niger State Government has assured residents that no Ebola case has been detected in the state, saying it has activated emergency response measures to prevent a possible outbreak. The Director of Public Health in the state Ministry of Health, Dr Ibrahim Idris, gave the assurance on Wednesday during a telephone conversation with our correspondent. Idris said the state was on high alert because of its proximity to the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), where a Ugandan woman was reportedly arrested over suspected exposure to Ebola. He urged residents to remain calm, continue their normal activities and observe necessary health precautions. The director said no person identified as a contact of the suspected case had entered Niger State, adding that the government was taking preventive measures to keep the disease out. Although Niger shares a boundary with the FCT, Idris said the state had not recorded any Ebola case and was strengthening its preparedness because of the severity of the disease. “Niger State has no Ebola outbreak, and the citizens should stay calm. We have already activated the emergency operation, and we will ensure that there is no outbreak of Ebola in the state,” he said. Idris said the state was monitoring the situation and taking steps to prevent people identified as contacts of the woman from introducing the disease into the state. “The state is doing everything to ensure that the 44 contacts said to have met the Ugandan woman do not enter Niger State. We have already activated our emergency operation. We will not give the disease any chances,” he said. He disclosed that the state held a high-level health meeting on Wednesday to assess its response measures, with particular attention to the reported Ebola concern in the FCT. The director urged residents to observe basic hygiene measures, including regular handwashing, and follow relevant public health advice. He also disclosed that the state was nearing completion of an isolation centre as part of measures to strengthen its preparedness for any suspected case. “As I am talking to you, we have almost completed our isolation centre, and we are putting other measures in place. We don’t want to leave anything to chance,” Idris said. Comments expressed here do not reflect the opinions of Vanguard newspapers or any employee thereof
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/no-e.title_zh: 尼日尔没有埃博拉 该州处于高度戒备状态
https://www.vanguardngr.com/2026/10/no-e.body_zh: 尼日尔州政府向居民保证，该州尚未发现任何埃博拉病例，并表示已启动应急响应措施以防止可能暴发疫情。该州卫生部公共卫生司司长易卜拉欣·伊德里斯博士周三在与本报记者的电话交谈中作出上述保证。伊德里斯说，由于该州与联邦首都区（FCT）相邻，因此处于高度戒备状态，据报一名乌干达妇女因疑似接触埃博拉病毒而在联邦首都区被捕。他敦促居民保持冷静，继续正常活动，并遵守必要的健康预防措施。司长表示，尚未有被确定为疑似病例接触者的人进入尼日尔州，并补充说政府正在采取预防措施以阻止该疾病传入。尽管尼日尔州与联邦首都区接壤，但伊德里斯表示该州尚未记录任何埃博拉病例，并且由于该疾病的严重性，正在加强 preparedness。“尼日尔州没有埃博拉疫情，公民应保持冷静。我们已经启动了应急行动，并将确保州内不会暴发埃博拉疫情，”他说。伊德里斯表示，该州正在监测局势，并采取措施防止被确定为该妇女接触者的人将疾病传入该州。“该州正在尽一切努力确保据称与乌干达妇女接触的44名接触者不会进入尼日尔州。我们已经启动了应急行动。我们不会给疾病任何机会，”他说。他透露，该州周三召开了一次高级别卫生会议，以评估其应对措施，特别关注联邦首都区报告的埃博拉担忧。司长敦促居民遵守基本卫生措施，包括定期洗手，并遵循相关的公共卫生建议。他还透露，作为加强应对任何疑似病例准备工作的一部分，该州即将完成一个隔离中心。“就在我与你交谈之际，我们的隔离中心已接近完工，我们正在落实其他措施。我们不想留下任何侥幸，”伊德里斯说。此处表达的评论不代表先锋报或其任何员工的意见

https://www.myjoyonline.com/contract-min.summary: The Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources has announced three additional safeguards to protect workers’ wages, benefits and conditions of service as mining companies transition from owner mining to contract mining. In a statement signed by the Ministry’s Director of Communications, Zambaga Rufai Saminu, the government said the measures were intended to guide the effective implementation of Ghana’s contract mining policy while safeguarding workers’ rights and welfare.
https://www.myjoyonline.com/contract-min.summary_zh: 土地和自然资源部宣布了三项额外保障措施，以保护工人在采矿公司从自营采矿转向合同采矿过渡期间的工资、福利和服务条件。该部通讯主任赞巴加·鲁法伊·萨米努签署的一份声明称，政府表示这些措施旨在指导加纳合同采矿政策的有效实施，同时保障工人的权利和福利。
https://www.myjoyonline.com/contract-min.body: The Ministry of Lands and Natural Resources has announced three additional safeguards to protect workers’ wages, benefits and conditions of service as mining companies transition from owner mining to contract mining. The measures require the Minerals Commission to prevent deterioration in workers’ employment conditions, harmonise remuneration across the mining industry value chain and categorise eligible mining contractors according to their capacity to provide mining-related services. In a statement signed by the Ministry’s Director of Communications, Zambaga Rufai Saminu, the government said the measures were intended to guide the effective implementation of Ghana’s contract mining policy while safeguarding workers’ rights and welfare. The Minerals Commission has been directed to complete the processes required to implement the measures and submit the necessary documents for approval by November 30, 2026. The Minerals Commission must ensure that no worker engaged, or to be engaged, by a mining contractor or similar service provider suffers any deterioration or reduction in wages, emoluments, entitlements, benefits or conditions of service because of the transition from owner mining to contract mining. The government has also affirmed that workers employed under contract mining arrangements should enjoy salaries, wages, allowances, benefits and other incentives equivalent to those applicable to owner mining workers performing comparable work before the transition. The Commission is required to take the necessary steps to harmonise salaries, wages and conditions of service across the mining industry value chain. The measure is intended to address concerns raised by the Ghana Mineworkers Union, human resource experts and other stakeholders about the potential impact of the transition on workers’ remuneration and welfare. Eligible contractors must be categorised according to their capacity to provide mining-related services. The Ministry said the new measures supplement existing regulatory requirements and do not prevent the Minerals Commission from taking further lawful action to advance the objectives of the Minerals and Mining (Local Content and Local Participation) Regulations, 2020 (LI 2431). The additional safeguards follow consultations involving the Ministry, the Minerals Commission, the leadership of the Ghana Mineworkers Union, industry experts and other relevant stakeholders. The Ministry said the engagements had clarified the regulatory and policy basis of the contract mining directive and reaffirmed the government’s position that workers must not be disadvantaged by its implementation. “The Ghanaian contract mining worker shall enjoy salaries, wages, allowances, benefits and other incentives equivalent to those applicable to an owner mining worker performing comparable work before the transition to contract mining,” the statement said. The Ministry acknowledged concerns about the possible unintended effects of the transition on salaries, wages and conditions of service, although it noted that most multinational mining companies operating in Ghana had successfully transitioned their operations to comply with the local content requirement. Under the policy, indigenous Ghanaian companies are required to undertake contract mining for surface mining operations. For underground operations, contract mining must be undertaken through a partnership in which a Ghanaian-owned company holds at least a 50 per cent interest. The requirement was incorporated into the sixth edition of the Local Procurement List, effective January 1, 2025, pursuant to LI 2431. The Ministry said the experience of multinational mining companies that had transitioned to comply demonstrated that the local content requirement was practicable and enjoyed broad industry support. The Ministry also warned against conduct that could undermine local content objectives or operate to the detriment of Ghanaian workers. It said the government would maintain “ZERO TOLERANCE” for unfair labour practices, cartelisation, bid rigging, fronting and any other conduct that undermines genuine Ghanaian participation or harms workers. The statement said the government, under President John Dramani Mahama’s Reset Agenda, remained committed to fairness, transparency, genuine Ghanaian participation and the protection of workers across the mining industry value chain. The Minerals Commission is expected to conclude the necessary implementation processes and submit the requisite documents for approval by November 30, 2026
https://www.myjoyonline.com/contract-min.title_zh: 合同采矿：以下是政府保护矿工的3项新措施
https://www.myjoyonline.com/contract-min.body_zh: 加纳土地和自然资源部宣布了三项额外保障措施，以保护工人在矿业公司从自营采矿转向合同采矿过渡期间的工资、福利和服务条件。这些措施要求矿产委员会防止工人就业条件恶化，统一矿业产业链各环节的薪酬，并根据提供采矿相关服务的能力对合格的采矿承包商进行分类。在由该部通讯主任赞巴加·鲁法伊·萨米努签署的一份声明中，政府表示这些措施旨在指导加纳合同采矿政策的有效实施，同时保障工人的权利和福利。矿产委员会已被指示完成实施这些措施所需流程，并在2026年11月30日前提交必要文件以供批准。矿产委员会必须确保任何受雇或将受雇于采矿承包商或类似服务提供商的工人，不会因从自营采矿转向合同采矿而遭受工资、薪酬、应享权利、福利或服务条件的任何恶化或降低。政府还确认，根据合同采矿安排雇用的工人应享有与过渡前从事类似工作的自营采矿工人相当的薪水、工资、津贴、福利和其他激励。委员会需采取必要步骤，统一矿业产业链各环节的薪水、工资和服务条件。该措施旨在解决加纳矿工工会、人力资源专家和其他利益相关者对过渡可能影响工人薪酬和福利提出的关切。合格承包商必须根据其提供采矿相关服务的能力进行分类。该部表示，这些新措施是对现有监管要求的补充，并不阻止矿产委员会采取进一步合法行动，以推进2020年《矿产和采矿（本地内容和本地参与）条例》（LI 2431）的目标。这些额外保障措施是在该部、矿产委员会、加纳矿工工会领导层、行业专家和其他相关利益相关者参与磋商后提出的。该部表示，这些互动澄清了合同采矿指令的监管和政策基础，并重申了政府的立场，即工人不得因其实施而处于不利地位。“加纳合同采矿工人应享有与过渡到合同采矿前从事类似工作的自营采矿工人相当的薪水、工资、津贴、福利和其他激励，”声明说。该部承认对过渡可能对薪水、工资和服务条件产生意外影响的担忧，尽管它指出，在加纳经营的大多数跨国矿业公司已成功转型其业务，以符合本地内容要求。根据该政策，加纳本土公司需承担露天采矿作业的合同采矿。对于地下作业，合同采矿必须通过合作伙伴关系进行，其中加纳拥有的公司至少持有50%的权益。该要求已纳入第六版本地采购清单，自2025年1月1日起生效，根据LI 2431。该部表示，已转型以符合要求的跨国矿业公司的经验表明，本地内容要求是可行的，并得到行业广泛支持。该部还警告不得进行可能破坏本地内容目标或损害加纳工人的行为。它表示，政府将对不公平劳工做法、卡特尔化、投标操纵、挂名参与以及任何其他破坏真正加纳参与或伤害工人的行为保持“零容忍”。声明说，在总统约翰·德拉马尼·马哈马的重置议程下，政府仍致力于公平、透明、真正的加纳参与以及保护矿业产业链各环节的工人。矿产委员会预计将在2026年11月30日前完成必要的实施流程并提交所需文件以供批准。

https://leadership.ng/plateau-indigenous.summary: Speaking for the coalition, President of the Berom Youths Moulder-Association and Coordinator of Indigenous Youth Nationalities, Northern Zone, Dalyop Mwantiri, accused Fulani groups of attempting to undermine joint security operations through petitions and social media campaigns. https://leadership.ng/plateau-indigenous.summary_zh: 代表联盟发言的贝罗姆青年塑造者协会主席兼北方区土著青年民族协调员达廖普·姆万蒂里，指责富拉尼团体试图通过请愿和社会媒体活动破坏联合安全行动。这些青年团体表示，这些活动是一种可能使武装分子受益的干扰，并呼吁联邦政府维持正在进行的安全行动，同时调查任何不当行为的指控。
https://leadership.ng/plateau-indigenous.body: The coalition, comprising Afizere, Anaguta, Atakar, Atten, Bache, Berom, Gamai, Irigwe, Kunlere, Mushere, Mwaghavul, Ron, Pan, Tarok and other ethnic youth bodies, stated this during a press conference at the Nigerian Union of Journalists (NUJ) FCT Secretariat in Abuja on Wednesday. Speaking for the coalition, President of the Berom Youths Moulder-Association and Coordinator of Indigenous Youth Nationalities, Northern Zone, Dalyop Mwantiri, accused Fulani groups of attempting to undermine joint security operations through petitions and social media campaigns. He called on the federal government to protect the DSS, Mobile Police Force and Operation Rainbow from what the coalition described as political and criminal pressure. The youth bodies said the campaigns were a distraction that could benefit militants and called on the Federal Government to sustain ongoing security operations while investigating any allegations of wrongdoing. “The petitioners alleged that the DSS should be held responsible for killings and abduction of members of the Fulani community, rustling of cattle, poisoning and shootings of cows, amongst several other crimes in Plateau state. “In addition, there is a video, to the same effect, making the rounds on many social media handles, including Facebook, claiming that the DSS, Mobile Police and Operation Rainbow are not serving the interest of peace on the Plateau EXCEPT for the Nigerian Army alone,” they stated. The coalition said the petition and video were intended to distort the facts and mislead Federal Government authorities and the general public. It also claimed that joint operations by the DSS, Mobile Police Force and Operation Rainbow had exposed a pattern in which cattle were allegedly grazed alongside armed militants who attacked and occupied communities. The group alleged that at least 152 hamlets, villages and communities had suffered such attacks. The coalition reiterated that Damian and the DSS were not involved in killings or cattle rustling, saying cattle intercepted while grazing on farmlands were held pending the identification of their owners and the alleged perpetrators. The coalition also alleged that Fulani militants had continued to ambush security operatives, citing the June 1, 2026, attack on a newly deployed DSS base at Nding Sesut, Fan, in Barkin Ladi Local Government Area, as well as the August 23, 2026, attack on Tanjol and Tarai villages in Jol community. It is alleged that more than 400 militants attacked the communities, ambushed and killed two DSS officers, and took away their rifles before retreating to Rankum, in the Mahanga area of Riyom Local Government Area. The group further alleged that Mobile Police Force officers were killed two weeks ago in Dares and Kwi villages in Bokkos and Riyom Local Government Areas, respectively. The group also claimed that the Operations Officer of Operation Rainbow, DSP David Babale, was ambushed and killed near a military checkpoint around Rakok village, on the outskirts of Barkin Ladi. The group called for a thorough investigation into allegations of unprofessional conduct, compromise and collusion involving some Army personnel. It warned that any demand for the withdrawal of the DSS, Mobile Police Force and Operation Rainbow from Plateau State would amount to support for the continuation of attacks and displacement. https://leadership.ng/plateau-indigenous.body_zh: 该联盟由阿菲泽雷、阿纳古塔、阿塔卡尔、阿滕、巴切、贝罗姆、加迈、伊里格韦、昆莱雷、穆谢雷、姆瓦加武尔、罗恩、潘、塔罗克和其他民族青年团体组成，周三在阿布贾尼日利亚记者工会（NUJ）联邦首都区秘书处举行的新闻发布会上发表了上述声明。代表联盟发言的贝罗姆青年塑造者协会主席兼北方区土著青年民族协调员达约普·姆万蒂里指责富拉尼团体试图通过请愿书和社交媒体活动破坏联合安全行动。他呼吁联邦政府保护国家安全局、机动警察部队和彩虹行动免受联盟所描述的政治和犯罪压力。这些青年团体表示，这些活动是一种可能让武装分子受益的干扰，并呼吁联邦政府维持正在进行的安全行动，同时调查任何不当行为的指控。“请愿者声称国家安全局应对富拉尼社区成员被杀和被绑架、牛只偷盗、投毒和射杀牛只以及高原州其他几起犯罪负责。“此外，还有一段视频在许多社交媒体账号上传播，包括Facebook，声称国家安全局、机动警察和彩虹行动没有为高原和平服务，除了尼日利亚军队之外，”他们表示。该联盟称，请愿书和视频旨在歪曲事实并误导联邦政府当局和公众。它还声称，国家安全局、机动警察部队和彩虹行动的联合行动暴露了一种模式，即牛只据称与武装分子一起放牧，这些武装分子袭击并占领社区。该团体声称至少有152个小村庄、村庄和社区遭受了此类袭击。该联盟重申达米安和国家安全局没有参与杀戮或偷牛，并表示拦截在农田放牧的牛只会被扣留，直到确定其主人和所谓肇事者。该联盟还指责富拉尼武装分子继续伏击安全人员，援引2026年6月1日对巴尔金拉迪地方政府区范区恩丁塞苏特新部署的国家安全局基地的袭击，以及2026年8月23日对乔尔社区坦乔尔和塔赖村庄的袭击。据称有超过400名武装分子袭击了这些社区，伏击并杀害了两名国家安全局官员，夺走他们的步枪，然后撤退到里约姆地方政府区马汉加地区的兰库姆。该团体进一步指称，机动警察部队官员两周前分别在博科斯和里约姆地方政府区的达雷斯和奎村被杀。该团体还声称，彩虹行动行动官戴维·巴巴莱警司在巴尔金拉迪郊区拉科克村附近的一个军事检查站附近遭到伏击并被杀。该团体呼吁对涉及一些军队人员不专业行为、妥协和勾结的指控进行彻底调查。它警告说，任何要求从高原州撤出国家安全局、机动警察部队和彩虹行动的做法都相当于支持继续袭击和流离失所。它敦促博拉·蒂努布总统和其他联邦政府当局不要屈服于它所描述的操纵。我们拥有优势。获取实时报道、突发独家新闻和独家视角，直接发送到您的手机。不要满足于陈旧新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS的WhatsApp，获取24/7更新→

https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.summary_zh: 信实工业有限公司董事长兼总经理穆克什·安巴尼周三在该公司贾姆讷格尔炼油厂——全球最大炼油综合体——欢迎美国国务卿马可·鲁比奥，并向他概述了公司在能源和数字基础设施领域的投资。美国驻印度大使塞尔吉奥·戈尔陪同鲁比奥前往贾姆讷格尔，该公司声明称这里是全球最大炼油厂所在地。信实工业执行董事阿南特·安巴尼也接待了来访者。
https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.body: Reliance Industries Ltd chairman and managing director Mukesh Ambani on Wednesday welcomed US secretary of state Marco Rubio at RIL’s Jamnagar refinery – the world’s largest refinery complex -- and gave him an overview of the company’s investments across energy and digital infrastructure. US ambassador to India Sergio Gor accompanied Rubio to Jamnagar, the home to the world’s largest refinery, a company statement said. The refinery is the largest and most complex single-site refinery in the world. It has 1.4 million barrels per day (mmbpd) crude processing capacity and a complexity index of 21.1, which is the highest in the world. The complexity index allows it to process even heaviest crude oils with almost zero waste. The visitors were given a tour of the world-class refinery complex, offering a first-hand view of its scale, advanced technology and integrated operations, the statement said. Visitors were also hosted by RIL executive director Anant Ambani. Rubio and Gor were also explained Reliance’s New Energy giga-factories, which are currently being commissioned in phases, and the data centres under construction. The tour provided an overview of the company’s investments across energy and digital infrastructure, bringing together its well-established advanced manufacturing and deep-tech capabilities, the statement said. Ambanis outlined Reliance’s long-term vision for the Jamnagar complex and its development as a centre for deep-tech, innovation and advanced manufacturing, it said. “The visit included wide-ranging discussions on the global energy landscape and opportunities for commercial partnerships across conventional and new energy,” it said. “The exchange covered reliable and affordable energy supplies, technological advances, resilient supply chains and the investment required to meet growing demand,” it added. Discussions also explored the increasing intersection of energy and digital infrastructure, including the role of dependable power in supporting data centres and the expansion of the digital economy, according to the statement. Ambanis shared their perspectives on opportunities for collaboration with US companies, drawing on complementary strengths in technology, engineering and advanced manufacturing. The interaction provided a constructive opportunity to exchange industry perspectives and explore areas of mutual commercial interest, the statement said
https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.title_zh: 美国国务卿马可·鲁比奥在贾姆纳格尔炼油厂会见穆克什·安巴尼和阿南特·安巴尼
https://www.hindustantimes.com/india-new.body_zh: 信实工业有限公司董事长兼总经理穆克什·安巴尼周三在信实工业贾姆纳格尔炼油厂——全球最大的炼油厂综合体——欢迎美国国务卿马可·鲁比奥，并向他概述了该公司在能源和数字基础设施领域的各项投资。美国驻印度大使塞尔吉奥·戈尔陪同鲁比奥前往贾姆纳格尔，这里的炼油厂是全球最大的炼油厂，公司声明称。该炼油厂是世界上规模最大、最复杂的单一厂址炼油厂。其原油日加工能力为140万桶，复杂性指数为21.1，是全球最高。这一复杂性指数使其能够加工最重的原油且几乎实现零浪费。来访者参观了这座世界级炼油厂综合体，亲眼看到其规模、先进技术和一体化运营，公司声明称。来访者还受到信实工业执行董事阿南特·安巴尼的接待。鲁比奥和戈尔还听取了关于信实新能源大型工厂的介绍，这些工厂目前正在分阶段投产，以及正在建设的数据中心。此次参观概述了该公司在能源和数字基础设施领域的投资，将其成熟的先进制造和深科技能力结合在一起，公司声明称。安巴尼家族概述了信实对贾姆纳格尔综合体的长期愿景，以及将其发展为深科技、创新和先进制造中心的目标，声明称。“此次访问包括就全球能源格局以及在传统能源和新能源领域开展商业伙伴关系的机会进行了广泛讨论，”声明称。“交流内容涵盖可靠且负担得起的能源供应、技术进步、 resilient供应链以及满足不断增长的需求所需的投资，”声明补充道。讨论还探讨了能源与数字基础设施日益增加的交汇点，包括可靠电力在支持数据中心和数字经济扩张方面的作用，声明称。安巴尼家族分享了他们对与美国公司开展合作机会的看法，这些合作基于双方在技术、工程和先进制造方面的互补优势。此次互动提供了一个建设性的机会来交流行业观点并探索共同的商业利益领域，声明称。

The assurance forms part of additional policy measures announced by the Ministry to guide the implementation of Ghana’s contract mining policy and address concerns about its potential impact on workers. In a statement signed by the Ministry’s Director of Communications, Zambaga Rufai Saminu, the government said it had taken account of concerns raised by the Ghana Mineworkers Union, human resource experts and other stakeholders over the possible effects of the transition on workers’ remuneration and welfare. The Ministry and the Minerals Commission have been holding consultations with the Union’s leadership, industry experts and other relevant stakeholders. According to the statement, the engagements clarified the regulatory and policy basis of the directive and reaffirmed the government’s position that workers must not be made worse off under the new arrangements. To enforce the safeguards, the government has directed the Minerals Commission to ensure that no worker engaged, or to be engaged, by a mining contractor or similar service provider suffers any deterioration or reduction in wages, emoluments, entitlements, benefits or conditions of service because of the transition. The Commission has also been instructed to take steps to harmonise salaries, wages and conditions of service across the mining industry value chain. Another measure requires eligible contractors to be categorised according to their capacity to provide mining-related services. The Ministry said the measures supplemented existing regulatory requirements and did not preclude further lawful action by the Minerals Commission to advance the objectives of the Minerals and Mining (Local Content and Local Participation) Regulations, 2020 (LI 2431). The Commission is expected to complete the processes required to implement the measures and submit the necessary documents for approval by November 30, 2026. The government also reaffirmed the local content requirements governing contract mining in Ghana. Under the policy, indigenous Ghanaian companies are to undertake contract mining for surface mining operations. Underground contract mining must be undertaken through partnerships in which Ghanaian-owned companies hold at least a 50 per cent interest. The requirement was incorporated into the sixth edition of the Local Procurement List, which took effect on January 1, 2025, pursuant to LI 2431. The Ministry said most multinational mining companies operating in Ghana had successfully transitioned their operations to comply with the requirement. It described the experience as evidence that the local content requirement was practicable and enjoyed broad industry support. However, it acknowledged that the transition had raised concerns about the possible implications for workers’ pay and conditions of service, prompting further consultations and the introduction of additional safeguards. The Ministry said the government would not tolerate practices that undermine local content objectives or disadvantage Ghanaian workers. It specifically warned against unfair labour practices, cartelisation, bid rigging, fronting and other conduct that could undermine genuine Ghanaian participation in the mining industry. Under President John Dramani Mahama’s Reset Agenda, the government said it remained committed to fairness, transparency, genuine Ghanaian participation and the protection of workers across the mining industry value chain. The Ministry said the additional measures were intended to ensure that the implementation of the contract mining policy promoted local participation while safeguarding the rights, remuneration and welfare of mineworkers
https://www.myjoyonline.com/no-mineworke.title_zh: 任何矿工都不应在合同采矿政策下受苦
https://www.myjoyonline.com/no-mineworke.body_zh: 政府已向矿工保证，在矿业公司从自营采矿过渡到合同采矿的过程中，任何雇员的工资、福利或服务条件都不应降低。土地和自然资源部表示，矿业承包商雇用的工人必须获得与过渡前从事类似工作的自营采矿工人所享有的同等薪水、工资、津贴、福利和其他激励措施。这一保证是该部宣布的额外政策措施的一部分，旨在指导加纳合同采矿政策的实施，并解决对其可能对工人产生的影响的担忧。在由该部通讯主任赞巴加·鲁法伊·萨米努签署的声明中，政府表示已考虑到加纳矿工工会、人力资源专家和其他利益相关者对过渡可能对工人工资和福利产生的影响所提出的担忧。该部和矿产委员会一直与工会领导层、行业专家和其他相关利益相关者进行磋商。根据声明，这些互动澄清了该指令的监管和政策基础，并重申了政府的立场，即在新安排下工人不得处于不利境地。为执行这些保障措施，政府已指示矿产委员会确保任何受雇或将受雇于矿业承包商或类似服务提供商的工人，不会因过渡而在工资、薪酬、权利、福利或服务条件方面遭受任何恶化或降低。该委员会还被指示采取步骤，协调整个矿业产业链的薪水、工资和服务条件。另一项措施要求根据提供采矿相关服务的能力对合格承包商进行分类。该部表示，这些措施补充了现有的监管要求，并不排除矿产委员会为推进《2020年矿产和采矿（本地内容和本地参与）条例》（LI 2431）的目标而采取进一步合法行动。预计该委员会将在2026年11月30日前完成实施这些措施所需的过程，并提交必要的文件以供批准。政府还重申了管辖加纳合同采矿的本地内容要求。根据该政策，加纳本土公司将承担露天采矿作业的合同采矿。地下合同采矿必须通过合作伙伴关系进行，其中加纳拥有的公司至少持有50%的权益。该要求已被纳入第六版本地采购清单，该清单根据LI 2431于2025年1月1日生效。该部表示，在加纳经营的大多数跨国矿业公司已成功过渡其业务以符合该要求。它将这一经验描述为证据，证明本地内容要求是可行的，并得到广泛的行业支持。然而，它承认过渡引发了对工人工资和服务条件可能产生的影响的担忧，从而促使进行进一步磋商并引入额外的保障措施。该部表示，政府不会容忍破坏本地内容目标或使加纳工人处于不利地位的行为。它特别警告不要采取不公平的劳工做法、卡特尔化、投标操纵、挂名参与和其他可能破坏加纳人在采矿业真正参与的行为。在总统约翰·德拉马尼·马哈马的重置议程下，政府表示仍致力于公平、透明、加纳人的真正参与以及保护整个矿业产业链的工人。该部表示，这些额外措施旨在确保合同采矿政策的实施在促进本地参与的同时，保障矿工的权利、薪酬和福利。

https://leadership.ng/utme-only-108-of-3.summary_zh: 教育部长图恩吉·阿拉乌萨博士周三在阿布贾接待2026年统一招生考试中得分最高的两位考生和其他六名杰出未成年考生时披露了这一信息。他解释说，寻求入学的未成年考生必须满足若干严格条件。阿拉乌萨透露，只有391名未成年考生在统一招生考试中至少获得320分，而进一步评估将有资格可能被录取的人数减少到108人。
https://leadership.ng/utme-only-108-of-3.body: The Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, disclosed this on Wednesday in Abuja while receiving the two highest-scoring candidates and six other outstanding underage candidates in the 2026 UTME. The candidates were presented to the minister by the Registrar of the Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB), Prof. Segun Aina. Alausa said the screening process was designed to ensure that exceptionally gifted children seeking admission before the minimum age of 16 demonstrated not only outstanding academic performance but also the psychological, emotional and intellectual maturity required for university education. According to the minister, 2,244,149 candidates registered for the 2026 UTME, while 2,174,396 sat the examination. About 39,000 of those who took the examination were below the prescribed minimum age for admission, 16. He explained that underage candidates seeking admission had to meet several rigorous conditions. These included scoring at least 320 out of 400 in the UTME (80 per cent) and obtaining at least 80 per cent in their post-UTME examinations. They were also required to attain the stipulated 80 per cent threshold in the assessment of their O-level results and pass a screening exercise to determine their psychological, emotional and intellectual readiness for higher education. Alausa disclosed that only 391 underage candidates scored at least 320 in the UTME, while further assessments reduced the number eligible for possible admission to 108. He described the successful candidates as exceptionally gifted, noting that they represented approximately 0.005 per cent of the candidates who sat the examination. “You are the geniuses in our society,” the minister told the students, stressing that the government had a responsibility to identify exceptional talents and nurture them into innovators capable of developing solutions to Nigeria’s challenges and those of the wider world. The minister clarified that the minimum admission age of 16 was not intended to frustrate academically gifted children or deny them opportunities to advance their education. Rather, he said the policy was designed to ensure that candidates admitted at a younger age possessed the maturity needed to cope with university life. He noted that feedback from the screening exercise had been encouraging, particularly regarding the candidates’ confidence, intellectual abilities and responses to questions designed to assess their preparedness for higher education. According to him, exceptional academic performance alone cannot justify early admission, as university education also requires emotional stability and the ability to navigate social and intellectual challenges. Alausa urged the successful candidates to regard their academic abilities as a responsibility to society rather than merely an opportunity for early admission and personal advancement. “You are the ones who will change Nigeria and change the world with your innovations,” he said. The minister linked the recognition of exceptional young talents to Nigeria’s broader development prospects, describing the country’s youthful population as a significant resource that must be properly educated and harnessed. He put Nigeria’s population at an estimated 220 million, with an average age of 18.5 years, adding that about 70 per cent of the population was below 30. Alausa said the Federal Government’s education reforms were aimed at expanding opportunities for young Nigerians and strengthening the country’s capacity to transform their potential into innovations and solutions that could improve lives. He congratulated the candidates on behalf of President Bola Tinubu and the Federal Ministry of Education, expressing confidence that their abilities could yield breakthroughs benefiting millions of people. The eight recognised candidates, including the two highest scorers in the 2026 UTME, received plaques and certificates from the minister. https://leadership.ng/utme-only-108-of-3.title_zh: 统一招生考试：39000名未达年龄考生中仅有108人符合联邦政府录取标准
https://leadership.ng/utme-only-108-of-3.body_zh: 教育部长图吉·阿拉乌萨博士周三在阿布贾接见2026年统一 tertiary 入学考试中得分最高的两位考生和其他六名杰出未成年考生时披露了这一信息。这些考生由联合招生与入学委员会（JAMB）注册官塞贡·艾纳教授呈交给部长。阿拉乌萨表示，筛选流程旨在确保寻求在最低16岁入学年龄前入学的特别有天赋儿童不仅表现出色学术成绩，还具备大学教育所需的心理、情感和智力成熟度。据部长介绍，2026年统一 tertiary 入学考试有2244149名考生注册，而2174396人参加了考试。参加考试的人中约有39000人低于规定的最低入学年龄16岁。他解释说，寻求入学的未成年考生必须满足若干严格条件。其中包括在统一 tertiary 入学考试中至少获得400分中的320分（80%），并在入学后考试中至少获得80%。他们还必须在O级成绩评估中达到规定的80%门槛，并通过筛选活动以确定他们对高等教育的心理、情感和智力准备度。阿拉乌萨披露，只有391名未成年考生在统一 tertiary 入学考试中至少获得320分，而进一步评估将有资格可能入学的考生人数减少到108人。他将这些成功考生描述为特别有天赋，指出他们约占参加考试考生总数的0.005%。“你们是我们社会的天才，”部长告诉学生们，强调政府有责任识别特殊人才并培养他们成为能够为尼日利亚挑战以及更广阔世界挑战开发解决方案的创新者。部长澄清说，16岁的最低入学年龄并非旨在挫败学术上有天赋的儿童或剥夺他们推进学业的机会。相反，他表示该政策旨在确保在较年轻年龄入学的考生具备应对大学生活所需的成熟度。他指出，筛选活动的反馈令人鼓舞，特别是在考生信心、智力能力和对旨在评估他们高等教育准备度问题的回应方面。据他说，仅有出色学术表现不能证明提前入学的合理性，因为大学教育还需要情感稳定性和应对社会及智力挑战的能力。阿拉乌萨敦促成功考生将他们的学术能力视为对社会的责任，而不仅仅是提前入学和个人发展的机会。“你们是将用创新改变尼日利亚和改变世界的人，”他说。部长将对杰出年轻人才的认可与尼日利亚更广泛的发展前景联系起来，将该国年轻人口描述为必须妥善教育和利用的重要资源。他估计尼日利亚人口为2.2亿，平均年龄18.5岁，并补充说约70%的人口低于30岁。阿拉乌萨表示，联邦政府的教育改革旨在扩大尼日利亚年轻人的机会，并加强该国将他们的潜力转化为能够改善生活的创新和解决方案的能力。他代表博拉·蒂努布总统和联邦教育部向考生表示祝贺，并表示相信他们的能力能够产生惠及数百万人的突破。这八名获得认可的考生，包括2026年统一 tertiary 入学考试中得分最高的两人，从部长手中接收了奖牌和证书。奥沃耶·丹妮拉·杰苏敦辛以372分成为得分最高的考生，而恩韦雷·金斯利·伊肯纳以370分紧随其后。我们拥有优势。获取实时报道、突发独家新闻和独家视角，直接发送到您的手机。不要满足于陈旧新闻。加入LEADERSHIP NEWS的WhatsApp以获取24/7更新→
